Taiwan warns of forest fire risks as dry season begins
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:49:58 UTC
17:49:58 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency warned Thursday that the public should take extra care with fire as the dry season increases the risk of forest fires, particularly in central and southern Taiwan.
The agency said 390 forest fires, or 89% of the total recorded over the past decade, occurred between October and May, before the arrival of the plum rain season. Careless use of fire caused 97% of forest fires, underscoring the importance of prevention, per a press release.
The agency launched a public awareness campaign, “A Single Spark Destroys a Forest,” urging people visiting forests to avoid careless use of fire. To help the public assess local conditions, the agency operates the Forest Fire Risk Assessment System, which provides local fire risk forecasts for the next seven days.
When prolonged drought leaves forest-floor vegetation and other combustible material exceptionally dry, the agency may activate disaster-prevention cell broadcast alerts to warn people in affected areas. The agency urged the public to follow three rules: do not burn weeds, do not discard cigarette butts, and do not burn garbage.
Under Article 34 of the Forest Act, starting a fire in a forest area or forest protection zone without permission is prohibited. Violators can face fines of up to NT$600,000 (US$18,000).
Anyone who deliberately sets fire to another person’s forest faces three to 10 years in prison and may also be liable for civil damages, per the press release.
The agency offers a reward of NT$100,000 for reports of suspected criminal acts involving the burning of national or public forests that lead to the perpetrator being caught. A separate NT$5,000 reward may be given to the first person to report a forest fire, subject to applicable requirements.
Anyone who discovers a forest fire should immediately call the toll-free forest protection hotline at 0800-000930 or the fire department at 119. The agency urged the public to treat forest fire prevention as a shared responsibility and avoid leaving any potential ignition sources behind when visiting the mountains.

Storms Austen and Boelo leave cliffs up to 1.2 metres high on the Flemish coast
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:47:00 UTC
17:47:00 KST

Following autumn storms Austen and Boelo, cliffs have formed along the coast. On the beaches of the resorts of Blankenberge and Middelkerke, these cliffs are up to 1.2 metres high. The Maritime and Coastal Services Agency (MDK) is pulling them down using machinery. In Knokke-Heist, its was local council workers that levelled the cliffs.
Storms Austen and Boelo leave cliffs up to 1.2 metres high on the Flemish coast
The first autumn storm, Austen, swept across Belgium on Friday 23 October. The Royal Meteorological Institute (RMI) issued a code orange warning for gusts of up to 100 kilometres per hour. A day later, storm Boelo also swept across Belgium. A code yellow warning for wind was issued for the coast.
The effects of the storms are particularly clear on the beaches of Blankenberge and Middelkerke. There, experts identified cliffs up to 1.2 metres high, stretching over hundreds of metres. These are steep, almost vertical walls of sand. They form when waves wash away sand at the high-water mark during a storm.
Higher than 1 metre
The cliffs can be dangerous. They are not always clearly visible, meaning walkers could easily experience a nasty fall. “Sometimes the beach recovers naturally, thanks to the tides. If the cliffs are higher than 1 metre, we have to level them out with a machine,” explains Dries Derudder of the Maritime Services and Coast Agency(MDK). “That is now only the case in Blankenberge and Middelkerke.”
‘The cliffs will be levelled on Thursday or Friday at the latest, so that everything is safe in the run-up to the autumn half-term.’
Cliffs had also formed on the beach in Knokke-Heist. The largest were up to 2 metres high. There local council workers demolished the cliffs. “We’ve created a sort of passageway from the soft sand to the wet sand,” explains Bert De Brabandere, the alderman responsible for beaches. “People can walk there safely. In time, the water will wash away the cliffs.”

URDA, Spain – Rescuers picked through mangled carriages on Oct 29 in a grim search for victims of Spain’s second fatal high-speed train crash in 2026, as the death toll rose to 69 and hopes of finding further survivors faded.
After cranes worked through the night to lift parts of the wreckage of the Oct 28 crash, emergency workers were seen carrying what appeared to be a body wrapped in a blanket from one of the trains in the central Spanish province of Toledo.
Regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page said the death toll had risen to 69 people and that human remains had been found during overnight rescue efforts. Work now involved crane operations, particularly on a carriage that was still overturned.
“We do not believe there could be any more fatalities beneath that one, but I say this with caution,” he said.
Unions blame lack of funding
Meanwhile, train drivers in Spain went ahead with a previously planned strike to press for more investment in railway safety after what is Europe’s deadliest train accident since a 2013 derailment in Spain’s Santiago de Compostela.
“We will continue demanding the necessary measures to make this sector safe again... It must have all the safety systems required to maintain the quality standards we have always had,” said Diego Martin of the train drivers’ union SEMAF.
“We cannot tolerate, under any circumstances, this type of incident happening again. Everyone should be able to travel without the risk of suffering this kind of accident,” he added at Madrid’s Atocha railway station.
The crash, which followed another fatal accident in January involving the same rail companies on the same line, has also upended campaigning for a Nov 29 snap election, with the leaders of Spain’s two main parties suspending campaign events.
Spain’s government has declared three days of national mourning for those killed in the crash, which Transport Minister Oscar Puente said happened after several trains stopped due to a signal failure.
A state-run Renfe train was then authorised to proceed at normal speed, even though there was a stationary Iryo-operated train ahead, Puente said on Oct 28.
Unions have already blamed a lack of funding and will to improve safety, saying that talks after the accident in January were abandoned in April.
Meanwhile, the government has said that the decision to authorise the Renfe train to continue its journey was “inexplicable”.
Pope sends condolences
Pope Leo sent his condolences to the families of those killed, wished a speedy recovery to the injured and conveyed his support and comfort to all affected, the Vatican said, adding he had also encouraged rescue workers to continue their efforts.
Of those injured, the authorities said 57 remained in hospital.
The crash prompted a major operation, which Spain’s interior ministry said involved the deployment of more than 800 military and police personnel, over 200 vehicles, three helicopters, a mobile command post, drones, mounted units and search dogs.
As investigations began, a judge in Toledo barred anyone not involved in emergency, security, healthcare or judicial work from the crash site with a 2km exclusion zone in both directions along the Madrid-Seville high-speed rail line.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who travelled to Toledo to take part in a meeting to monitor and coordinate the emergency response, said the authorities were working “day and night” to support the victims and their families and to “get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy”.
Meanwhile, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, leader of the centre-right People’s Party, which is currently leading in polls, was due to visit the town of Urda, where local people rushed to help with rescue efforts in the aftermath of the crash.
Foreign nationals among casualties
Spain’s Foreign Ministry said 42 foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the crash, information available so far showed, of whom one was killed and at least seven injured.
The Oct 28 accident has added urgency to a debate about safety on Spain’s railways, Europe’s longest network and until recently a source of pride in the country.
Train drivers would go ahead with their strike to press for structural changes in railway safety, SEMAF said, adding that it was studying further action.
Renfe said the strike caused significant disruption to rail services, adding that passengers could change or cancel tickets free of charge and would be notified of affected services. REUTERS

Australia considering Iron Dome's Tamir interceptor for missile defense
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:44:54 UTC
17:44:54 KST

Australia is considering looking at Israel’s Iron Dome missile defense system as it works to build its first land-based ballistic missile shield.
According to local media, Australia’s Defense Ministry has approached Washington regarding cost and delivery timelines for the US Marine Corps’ Medium Range Intercept Capability, which uses the SkyHunter, a US-built version of the Iron Dome’s Tamir interceptors.
It is also looking at the Patriot and Aegis missile defense systems. Bids from Norway’s Kongsberg and South Korea’s Hanwha are also expected.
Canberra is looking for a medium-range missile defense system as Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles has called the current geopolitical situation “The most complex and threatening strategic circumstances” since World War II.
The Australian reported that a tender issued by the country’s Defense Ministry in mid-October wants a “proven” off-the-shelf system selected by the end of next year, followed by a live-firing during Exercise Talisman Sabre by 2029. According to the report, the planned system will not be fully operational until the middle of the 2030s.
Highly critical of Israel
Australia has been heavily critical of Israel’s war in Gaza. Canberra does not supply weapons to Israel, and its purchase of Israeli defence products continues to come under political scrutiny.
But while Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has insisted that the country does “not sell arms to Israel,” Defense Industry Minister Pat Conroy has defended the country’s use of Israeli military systems.
“We make no apology for getting the best possible equipment for the Australian Defence Force,” he said at the Indo-Pacific Maritime Exposition last year.
Environment Minister Murray Watt has also supported the decision to look at Israeli technology, telling the committee on Thursday that "the government will always seek to deliver the most suitable military technology.”
Integral part of Israel’s missile defense array
Initially designed to shoot down short-range rockets, the Iron Dome has become an integral component of Israel's multi-layered defense array over the last 15 years.
The system’s modular architecture enables seamless integration with additional defense layers, and it can operate independently or as part of Israel’s broader air defense network that includes the Arrow (Arrow 2 and Arrow 3) system, which intercepts ballistic missiles outside of the Earth’s atmosphere, and the David’s Sling missile defense system, which is designed to intercept tactical ballistic missiles, medium- to long-range rockets, and cruise missiles fired at ranges between 40 and 300 kilometers.
Iron Dome took part in a long series of conflicts and operations, from Operation Protective Edge, Operation Guardian of the Walls, Operation Breaking Dawn, Operation Shield and Arrow, Operation Swords of Iron, and Operations Rising and Roaring Lion, where it served alongside the Arrow and David’s Sling as a central pillar in the protection of Israel’s home front.
Each round of fighting was followed by a new wave of software updates, radar refinements, and interceptor improvements.
The system’s radar has been upgraded to track more targets simultaneously, its algorithms have become faster and more selective, and its interceptors were refined to handle longer ranges and more demanding engagement profiles.
Yet, despite its successes, the Iron Dome is not infallible.
Israeli officials have consistently noted that no air‑defense system can guarantee complete protection. Some rockets inevitably penetrate the system’s defenses, underscoring the importance of measures such as early warning sirens and reinforced shelters.
Nevertheless, the system’s high interception rate has significantly reduced casualties and property damage during periods of conflict, altering both military calculations and civilian life in Israel.

17:44:32 KST

The combination of artificial intelligence and quantum computing could accelerate advances in both technologies, potentially transforming industries ranging from healthcare to finance, according to senior Bank of America global strategist Haim Israel.
Israel, who heads the bank’s global thematic research team and is the most senior Israeli there, said advances in AI are helping researchers overcome longstanding technical challenges in quantum computing, while quantum technology could eventually address some of the processing limitations holding back AI development.
“We spent the last couple of years talking about AI, and while quantum was always there, it was in the background,” Israel told The Jerusalem Post. “But in the last two to three years, AI has allowed us to have a breakthrough.”
The bank estimates that the quantum computing industry, which has already surpassed $1 billion in annual revenue, could grow to approximately $15 billion by the end of the decade and $80 billion by 2035.
At the same time, the timeline for so-called Q-Day, the point at which quantum computers should become capable of breaking widely used encryption methods, is moving closer. According to Israel, Bank of America has brought its estimate forward to 2030.
Quantum computers operate differently from conventional computers, which process information using bits represented as either zero or one. Quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits. They exploit quantum-mechanical properties such as superposition to perform certain calculations in ways that are impractical for conventional systems.
The technology has long faced a central obstacle: qubits are highly sensitive to their surroundings, making them difficult to control and prone to errors. And unreliable results have limited the ability to scale quantum systems and use them for practical applications.
Israel said AI was helping researchers improve control over quantum systems and reduce error rates, marking a significant step toward more reliable machines.
“2022 was the inflection point with qubits going up and errors going down,” he said.
The relationship between the two technologies could become increasingly important as AI models grow in size and complexity. Training and operating advanced AI systems requires substantial computing resources, while quantum computers could eventually accelerate particular calculations that are difficult or expensive for conventional machines.
“AI helped build quantum, and quantum is bringing AI to the next level,” Israel said.
Israel said the industry was approaching an early development stage comparable to the period before the widespread adoption of ChatGPT brought generative AI to mainstream attention.
“We are before the ChatGPT moment of quantum,” he said.
Although quantum computing is at an early stage, Israel said the sector already has an established ecosystem of hardware and software developers, alongside start-ups working on encryption and related technologies. He said the industry was better positioned than AI had been at a comparable stage, although its commercial structure would be different.
But rather than becoming a widely distributed technology used by billions of people like AI, quantum computing is likely to remain concentrated in a relatively small number of highly specialized systems, he said.
Its potential applications span healthcare, financial services, chemicals, energy, industrial production, and logistics, where complex calculations could help companies improve efficiency, optimize processes, and accelerate research.
No regulation or intervention
Israel said the pace of development was raising questions about whether governments, regulators, and institutions were keeping up with the technology.
“There is not a lot of regulation, or government intervention,” he said, adding that responsibility for how these technologies are used ultimately rests with the people and institutions developing them.
He compared the issue to nuclear energy, which can be used to generate electricity but also produce weapons.
He said companies were already developing internal safeguards and best practices, while governments faced the challenge of responding to technologies advancing faster than existing regulatory frameworks.
For now, significant technical and commercial hurdles remain before quantum computing can deliver on its broadest promises. But as AI helps researchers improve quantum hardware and software, the two technologies are increasingly being developed in tandem, with potential consequences for scientific research, industrial productivity, and global cybersecurity.
“The technology is parve. It's a question of what we do with it,” Israel said. “If we use it in the right way, everything will change for the better. It’s up to us.”

US Justice Dept loses initial bid to block votes from alleged noncitizens in California

2026-10-29

17:44:06 KST

A US judge rejected on Wednesday a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections received from people on a list of more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens.
The decision marks the latest setback for President Donald Trump's effort to expand the federal government's role in elections ahead of the midterms, as his Republican Party faces a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress.
US District Judge David Carter issued the decision after a hearing on Tuesday in Los Angeles federal court over the Justice Department's request for a temporary restraining order barring officials from counting any ballots from the individuals it flagged.
The Justice Department filed the lawsuit on October 15, a rare intervention in the voting process weeks before an election.
California has said the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust. It said the Justice Department's assertions relied on "suspect data" and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters.
California judge blocks Trump bid to restrict mail-in votes
California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives (52) than any other state.
Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its "sanctuary state" policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by noncitizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare.
The hearing comes after a federal appeals court on Monday rejected an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule.
The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot.
Outside California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states with competitive races.
In Alaska, the Justice Department last week asked a judge to prevent certification of election results if the Republican incumbent senator loses by a slim margin, alleging that the presence of another candidate with a similar name on the ballot could confuse voters. Alaska has urged that the case be dismissed, arguing it has taken steps to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot.
In Washington state, the Justice Department sent a letter on Monday asking officials not to count ballots from 400 voters it said may not be citizens. Washington's top elections official said the timing of the request indicated it was intended to cast unfounded suspicion on election results.
State records show California had 23 million registered voters as of December 2025, while Washington had 5 million as of 2024.
Voting rights activists have expressed concern that the federal government's methods for scrutinizing state voter lists to identify noncitizen voters risk wrongly flagging naturalized citizens for removal from the rolls.

Türkiye’s auto sector targets record $45.5 billion in exports in 2027
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:40:06 UTC
17:40:06 KST

Türkiye’s automotive industry aims to increase its share in international markets and achieve a new export record of $45.5 billion in 2027, according to the 2027 Presidential Annual Program.
The program outlines efforts to align the automotive sector with the green and digital transformation driven by the evolving global mobility vision. It aims to strengthen domestic supply chains and technological development across all stages, from design to production.
Authorities also seek to increase the sector’s value-added output and enhance branding efforts to raise its share in global markets. Progress on actions and key projects under the Mobility Vehicle and Technologies Road Map will be monitored, and the action plan will be updated when necessary.
Work will continue to improve the reliability, response time and operational stability of autonomous driving functions. Studies will also focus on the low-latency transmission of camera and lidar sensor data.
Under the Hydrogen-Based Carbon-Neutral Internal Combustion Engine Development Project, work on the generator phase will continue, while efforts to develop a hydrogen-powered train will also proceed.
Three fuel-cell tests aimed at developing hydrogen fuel-cell and component technologies will continue. In addition, verification devices designed to test the performance of electric vehicle charging stations during both direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) charging will be trialed across all station types. Inspection criteria suited to the country’s AC and DC charging infrastructure capabilities will also be established and reported.
A roadmap covering charging infrastructure for all vehicle categories will be prepared, and state support mechanisms will be introduced. Companies investing in charging stations will receive support, while the charging network is set to expand nationwide.
Studies will also be carried out under the EU-backed SAFELOOP and STREAMS projects to develop technology and manufacturing capabilities in areas including batteries, sensors, electronic control units, digital instrument clusters, electric motor systems and automotive software.
Education curricula and teaching methods will be updated to meet current technological requirements. Programs implemented by the private sector to enhance national competitiveness will be supported, while entrepreneurs developing projects in educational technologies will be backed through various programs and events.
The automotive production index, which is expected to reach 129 by the end of this year, is projected to rise to 131 in 2027.
Increasing automotive exports and reducing imports remain among the sector’s key objectives. Automotive exports are expected to reach $41.6 billion by the end of this year and are targeted to increase to $45.5 billion in 2027.
Efforts are also continuing to reduce external dependence in the sector. Automotive imports are projected to total $37.7 billion this year and are not expected to exceed $39.5 billion in 2027.
Meanwhile, the automotive sector’s share of Türkiye’s manufacturing industry exports is expected to reach 16.5 percent in 2027.

Libya's eastern govt bars entry to Iranians and Afghans
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:40:01 UTC
17:40:01 KST

Breadcrumb
Libya's eastern administration bars entry to Iranians and Afghans
Libya’s eastern-based government banned the entry of Iranian and Afghan nationals through all land, sea and air ports, the government said late on Wednesday.
The move extends entry restrictions the eastern administration imposed on nationals of four African countries in June, in a country split between rival governments in the east and west since 2014.
The government did not give a reason for the decision.
"The nationals of both Iran and Afghanistan are prohibited from entering Libyan territory through all land, air, and sea ports of entry," the government said in a statement posted on its verified Facebook page.
It added that the Ministry of Interior would be responsible for implementing the decision and for deporting Iranian and Afghan nationals who do not hold valid residence permits.
Libya has become a transit route for migrants fleeing conflict and poverty to Europe across the Mediterranean since the fall in 2011 of dictator Muammar Gaddafi to a NATO-backed uprising. Factional conflict has split the country since 2014.
The Benghazi-based government of Osama Hamad is allied to military commander Khalifa Haftar, who controls the east and large areas of southern Libya.
The internationally recognised government of Abdulhamid Dbeibah, who came to power through a UN-backed process in 2021, is based in Tripoli.
In June, Hamad's government banned nationals of African countries–Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia and Somalia–citing a "reorganisation of foreign nationals’ entry to Libya".
The members of accredited diplomatic and consular missions and family members are exempted, the statement said. The same applies to those working in medical and educational professions, provided they have obtained work authorizations.
Libya is home to more than 900,000 migrants, according to UN data collected in June.

Naftogaz expands legal battle with Russia to the Arctic – WSJ
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
10:39:52 EET
17:39:52 KST

Naftogaz has taken its legal battle against Russia to the Arctic, setting a unique precedent for the world by securing the seizure of a Russian vessel, the U.S. publication The Wall Street Journal reports.
The seizure of the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov in the Svalbard archipelago was the result of a yearslong legal campaign by NJSC Naftogaz Ukrainy and could pave the way for compensation for other owners of assets expropriated by Russia, the publication said.
According to the WSJ, Naftogaz, together with law firm U.S. law firm Covington & Burling LLP, is conducting a global search for Russian state assets that can be seized to enforce an arbitration award concerning the company's assets in Crimea.
As the publication reported, the company has already secured the seizure of Russian real estate in Finland and Austria. The WSJ said that lawyers from Norwegian law firm Wikborg Rein, which represents Naftogaz in Norway, drew attention to the vessel, which was operating between Murmansk and the settlement of Barentsburg. They determined that the vessel was not covered by state immunity and prepared a court application in advance, before the vessel arrived in the archipelago.
The seizure was carried out on September 2 pursuant to a ruling by the Nord-Troms District Court," the WSJ reported.
Lawyers cited by the publication believe that the seizure, together with the ruling by the tribunal in The Hague, sets a precedent for other parties affected by Russian expropriation.
As Naftogaz Acting CEO Serhiy Fedorenko said, the significance of the seizure extends beyond the value of the vessel. According to him, the company will continue searching for Russian assets around the world until the compensation awarded to it has been paid in full.
As reported, in 2019, an arbitration tribunal in The Hague ruled that the Russian Federation had unlawfully expropriated Naftogaz's assets in Crimea. In April 2023, the tribunal awarded the company $4.2 billion in compensation plus interest, bringing the total to more than $5 billion.

Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:38:54 GMT
17:38:54 KST

Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
- Published
Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 69 people and injured dozens.
Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.
Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who travelled to the area of the crash, said authorities were working "day and night" to "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".
The release of the recordings comes as Spain begins three days of national mourning for one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.
One train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train run by private operator Iryo, with 147 passengers.
A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.
But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.
Audio recordings published by Spanish news outlets including El Pais and RTVE reveal the conversations that took place between the two train's drivers and the control centre in the Spanish capital ahead of the crash.
In one recording, a control centre operator is speaking to the driver of the Renfe train, which was travelling behind the other train and was having some technical difficulties.
After some exchanges, the control operator tells the driver: "Continue your journey and then proceed under [Lateral Signalling Block], at normal speed with normal operation."
The driver replies, "At normal speed?" To which the controller says: "Yes."
The Lateral Signaling Block is a back-up or alternative train system used when the automatic signalling or data transmission system fails.
The driver of the other train - operated by Iryo - says in another audio recording that communication with the train-control system has been lost and it is not moving.
The train "is stationary in front of the entry signal at Urda", the driver tells the control centre operator. After a series of exchanges, the driver is then told to "resume the journey" normally.
The Iryo driver then contacts the control centre again, according to a later recording, saying they cannot start the train. "The train won't allow me to control the [security] system. That's why I am still stopped in front of the entry signal," they say.
The latter recording suggests that the controller had been notified that the Iryo train remained stationary as the Renfe train approached.
Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by the other train.
Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente said on Wednesday that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was "inexplicable".
The leaking of the audio recordings has been criticised by some Spanish politicians.
Posting on X, Alberto Ibáñez, a member of Congress for the left-wing Sumar platform, described the leaks as "despicable".
Irene Montero - the prime ministerial candidate for the left-wing Podemos party - said responsibility for the crash should not be placed on one worker, adding that train drivers and experts have been warning against the liberalisation of the railway sector for years.
From the crash site, Sánchez said: "We are working day and night not only to support the victims' families, but also to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again."
Most Spanish politicians have cancelled all public engagements and suspended their campaigning ahead of a snap election on 29 November.
The exception is the far-right party Vox. Its leader, Santiago Abascal, said his party would not take part in what he described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure.
Overnight, around 1,500 people gathered outside the Spanish Transport Ministry building in the capital, according to Spanish broadcaster TVE, which reported that demonstrators were largely calling for the resignations of Sánchez and Puente.
Police used tear gas to disperse crowds after protesters hurled bottles and flares. No injuries or arrests were reported.
Rail drivers went ahead with a planned strike on Thursday, with the Spanish Union of Railway Drivers (Semaf) saying the strike action was being held "in defence of railway safety".
The leader of Spain's main opposition People's Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: "Spain has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure."
At the crash site, emergency crews worked through the night under powerful floodlights to cut open metal carriages in the search for victims, with many of those killed in the crash still to be identified.
Hundreds of personnel have been deployed to the disaster site to assist with recovery efforts, according to Spain's interior ministry, with drones and helicopters being used to find victims and remove rubble.
A spokesperson for the Spanish Civil Guard told the BBC they had deployed more than 900 people from different specialist departments, and the priority now was identifying remains.
They said they did not know how long this would take, but urged those with missing family members to go to one of the local centres which have been set up to offer DNA samples.
Witnesses of the crash described seeing people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.

Late on Wednesday, relatives were still trying to gather information about passengers who were on either of the trains.
The Spanish Civil Guard has set up bureaus in Madrid, Toledo, Seville and Córdoba to investigate reports of missing persons.
"The top priority is the identification of the missing persons and the taking of DNA samples to be able to locate their relatives," the civil guard wrote in a post on X.
Wednesday's crash is the worst the country has seen since 2013, when 80 people died on the outskirts of Santiago de Compostela in north-west Spain.

Details
This is the latest in a series of generals being dismissed, and it comes even as U.S. President Donald Trump is considering resuming strikes on Iran in the eight-month war.
U.S. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed as head of the Strategy, Plans and Policy Directorate of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff. He became the second general dismissed from the position, known in military circles as "J5," under Hegseth. His predecessor, Lieutenant General Joseph McGee, was forced to retire in October last year.
A Pentagon representative said there was no immediate replacement for Sylvia and that no reason for his dismissal had been provided.
A representative of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff said: "The Chairman, Joint Staff and Joint Force express their deep gratitude to Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia and his family for 32 years of distinguished service to our country" and "wish him and his family all the best."
Typically, the J5 director and his staff are responsible for developing and coordinating military plans with both the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the U.S. president. Sylvia’s dismissal came amid Trump’s repeated statements about launching new military operations against Iran.
Trump vowed to "finish what was started" in Iran after the war with Israel began eight months ago and said new strikes could take place after next week’s midterm elections.
According to two diplomats familiar with the situation, U.S. officials warned a number of Middle Eastern countries and regional allies that they needed to be prepared for the possible resumption of hostilities after Tuesday’s election, as well as possible retaliatory measures by Iran. They said Trump had not yet made a final decision on new strikes.
A third U.S. aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are heading to the region.

Algeria denies flying weapons over Poland on military aircraft
Algeria has denied allegations that its military aircraft transported weapons through Polish airspace, insisting that no dangerous materials were carried and that all flights complied with international aviation regulations.
The Algerian embassy in Warsaw issued a statement on Wednesday rejecting reports that Algerian aircraft had flown over Poland carrying weapons, describing the claims as false and urging the public to verify information through official sources.
"The information is incorrect," the embassy said, stressing that "no dangerous materials of any kind were transported aboard Algerian aircraft".
It called for information to be verified against official sources before being published.
The statement came in response to reports saying that Algerian aircraft were transporting weapons through Polish airspace, which included information attributed to the Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces.
The embassy said that "all flights by Algerian aircraft are conducted in accordance with relevant international and bilateral legal provisions, and after obtaining the necessary authorisations from the countries whose airspace they cross".
It also reaffirmed Algeria's commitment to strengthening relations with Poland, describing ties between the two countries as longstanding and expected to develop further.
Algerian military flight to Moscow
The controversy centres on a flight on 7 October, when an Algerian military aircraft reportedly departed from Boufarik Air Base near Algiers, bound for Moscow's Vnukovo Airport.
According to reports, the aircraft crossed Polish airspace after receiving the necessary authorisation from Polish authorities, following a request submitted by Algeria.
Polish media recently quoted Jacek Goryszewski, spokesperson for the Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces, as saying that the Algerian aircraft had obtained the required permits.
He also said Algerian authorities had not declared any dangerous materials aboard the aircraft.
According to the spokesperson, military aircraft belonging to countries outside the European Union and NATO must obtain prior authorisation before flying over Polish territory.
Such flights also require notification to the Polish Air Force, specifically its Air Operations Centre and Air Component Command.
Applications must be submitted using a standardised form detailing the nature of the flight and the cargo being transported.

Diesel deal with Russia fails to lower fuel prices in U.S.
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:36:42 UTC
17:36:42 KST

Fuel prices in the U.S. rose another seven cents after the announcement of the diesel deal with Russia, reaching $6.35 per gallon (about 3.8 liters), The Wall Street Journal reported, citing data from the American Automobile Association.
U.S. President Donald Trump announced October 9 that he had reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin on deliveries of Russian diesel fuel to world markets. The U.S. Treasury Department temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel until April 7, 2027, to implement the deal.
Trump said Russia would supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, another 500,000 tons in November, and an additional 1 million tons after that. The first tanker carrying Russian diesel fuel left the port of Primorsk on October 22, Reuters reported.
Experts have been skeptical that the diesel deal will significantly lower fuel prices in the U.S.
Midterm elections for Congress will take place in the U.S. on November 3. Analysts predict the Republican Party’s representation in both chambers will shrink as a result. Polling shows rising fuel prices have become one of the main sources of discontent among U.S. residents with the Republican administration led by Trump.

NATO urges allies to transfer Patriot missiles from stockpiles to Ukraine – deputy secretary general
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
10:36:41 EET
17:36:41 KST

NATO is calling on allied member states to urgently transfer air defense missiles to Ukraine, specifically PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot systems, without waiting for scheduled new production deliveries, stated NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Šekerinska.
"We have once again appealed to our allies and said: please go into your stockpiles. If you have PAC-2s, PAC-3s, please give them. If you have deliveries waiting to take place in the next few weeks or months, please give them to Ukraine now and then based on other sales, later deliveries, you can get your stocks replenished," Šekerinska emphasized during the special event "Support Ukraine, Defend Europe," organized by the newly established Kyiv Security Forum (KSF) Office in Brussels.
According to her, the need for additional air defense assets has become particularly acute due to the aggressor state's deployment of jet-powered drones. Therefore, NATO is urging allies to provide Ukraine not only with Patriot missiles but also with other interceptors, including AIM-9 missiles, components for SAMP/T systems, and 20mm ammunition.
Šekerinska noted that air defense shortages represent a global challenge. The defense industry is not yet keeping pace with the growing demands driven by Russia's war against Ukraine and other conflicts worldwide. "This is becoming probably the most important challenge that we are facing. How do we make sure that we reach our stockpiles and make everything possible available to Ukraine?" the NATO Deputy Secretary General pointed out.
She stressed that she personally raises this issue during every visit to allied capitals, that the NATO Secretary General echoes these same appeals, and that the transfer of weaponry to Ukraine is regularly discussed at North Atlantic Council meetings.
According to Šekerinska, 99% of the air defense assets used by Ukraine have been provided by NATO allies.
She also reported that arms deliveries under the PURL program—a mechanism for purchasing American weaponry for Ukraine using funds from European partners—are proceeding according to schedule.
"Let me be very clear. The delivery of PURL packages goes according to the schedule. We have delivered even more than what we have managed to finance because we know the urgency is extreme," Šekerinska noted.
The NATO Deputy Secretary General also reaffirmed allies' commitments to provide Ukraine with €70 billion in support in 2026 and at least the same amount in 2027. At the same time, she stressed that assistance decisions depend on allied states and their domestic procedures.
According to Šekerinska, NATO views cooperation with Ukraine as a two-way partnership in which allies not only provide assistance but also adopt the unique combat experience of Ukrainian service members. "Ukraine has been clearly in the forefront of modern warfare," the NATO Deputy Secretary General emphasized.
The special event "Support Ukraine, Defend Europe" took place with the participation of high-ranking officials from the European Union, NATO, and Ukraine. It was dedicated to strengthening support for Ukraine and shared European security.
This is the first high-level event organized by the KSF Office in the EU, which commenced operations in Brussels on the initiative of KSF Chairman and Prime Minister of Ukraine (2014–2016) Arseniy Yatsenyuk.

Russian Submarine Generalissimus Suvorov Launches Bulava Intercontinental Ballistic Missile
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:35:40 UTC
17:35:40 KST

Russia’s nuclear-powered submarine Generalissimus Suvorov has launched a Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile.
The launch was reported by Russia’s United Shipbuilding Corporation.
The launch may be intended to demonstrate the readiness of Russia’s nuclear forces and maintain military and political pressure on the international community.
The missile was launched in the Sea of Okhotsk.
The launch was carried out as part of the submarine crew’s combat training. The submarine is part of Russia’s Pacific Fleet.
The missile was aimed at Chizha test range in the Arkhangelsk region.
The Bulava is a submarine-launched intercontinental ballistic missile designed to arm Russia’s Project Borei nuclear-powered submarines.
The Generalissimus Suvorov belongs to Project 955A Borei-A and is a nuclear-powered strategic missile submarine.
The submarine was built at the Sevmash shipyard based on an upgraded design developed by Rubin Design Bureau.
Construction of the submarine began on December 26, 2014.
It belongs to the fourth generation of nuclear-powered submarines developed for the Russian Navy.
The naval flag was raised aboard the Generalissimus Suvorov on December 29, 2022.
The R-30 Bulava is a Russian three-stage submarine-launched ballistic missile designed for deployment aboard Project955 Borei nuclear-powered submarines.
Its development began in 1995, and it effectively entered service in 2017–2018.
The first- and second-stage sustainer engines use solid propellant. The third stage is equipped with a liquid-propellant engine to provide the required velocity and maneuverability during the final phase of the missile’s trajectory.
The missile is launched at an inclined angle, allowing the submarine to launch it while underway.
The guidance system is hybrid, combining celestial navigation with signals from Russia’s GLONASS satellite navigation system.
The missile also carries several decoys. Its primary warheads are capable of maneuvering in flight and adjusting their trajectories to improve their ability to penetrate missile defence systems.

Türkiye hosts 13th OTS summit to advance Turkic unity and cooperation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:33:53 UTC
17:33:53 KST

Türkiye is hosting the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Ankara to further “unity in language, thought, and deed” among its member states.
The summit kicked off on Thursday with the Meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the OTS.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hosted the meeting, according to diplomatic sources.
Foreign ministers of the OTS posed for a family photo ahead of the meeting.
The two-day summit is hosted by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan under the theme Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought and Deed.
Established in 2009, the OTS, formerly known as the Turkic Council, adopted its current name during its eighth summit held in the Turkish metropolis Istanbul in 2021.
While Türkiye, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan are members, Turkmenistan, Hungary, the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, and the Economic Cooperation Organization hold observer status.
The organisation said on October 24 that the summit will bring together the heads of state of its member states, as well as high-level representatives from observer states and its secretary general, to “discuss the current state and future prospects of cooperation within the Organization,” among other issues.
It said in a statement that the heads of state are expected to review the progress achieved across the OTS’ priority areas, and that particular emphasis will be placed on “further strengthening unity and solidarity” among the Turkic states and advancing cooperation under the Turkic World Vision 2040.
It added that the summit will also mark Türkiye’s assumption of the OTS’ chairmanship from Azerbaijan, and is expected to address the appointment of a new secretary general and the organisation’s strategic priorities “for the forthcoming period.”
“The Heads of State are expected to adopt the Ankara Declaration, together with a number of decisions and documents aimed at deepening cooperation and further strengthening the institutional framework of the OTS,” it added.
The leaders’ summit will be held on Friday.
‘Unity in deed’
Turan Gafarli, a non-resident fellow at the Baku-based Topchubashov Center, defined support among Turkic states and bolstering their political solidarity as the significant aspect of the Ankara summit.
Noting that they are living through a period in which the world faces “increasing uncertainty,” Gafarli told Anadolu that the Turkic world is evolving into a political structure that is “developing the capacity to act in unison in the face of international developments.”
“Naturally, this is a long-term process. Yet, the true meaning of brotherhood is not just coming together during good times, but standing by one another during difficult ones,” he said, noting his belief that the summit in Türkiye will further solidify the “atmosphere of trust built to date.”
Gafarli highlighted the term of unity used in the summit’s theme as “highly significant,” as well as expressed belief that the summit will give momentum to developments particularly in the realms of economic relations, transport corridors, and political coordination.
He stated the growing strategic importance of the Middle Corridor presented a “historic opportunity” for the Turkic states to become more closely interconnected economically, but that this requires a number of steps, including bolstering trade between member states.
“Furthermore, it is essential that the Turkic states engage in closer consultation on international issues and advocate more robustly for their shared interests,” he said, adding he believes Türkiye’s chairmanship could bring fresh dynamism in this context.
Meanwhile, Shairbek Dzhuraev, the president of the Crossroads Central Asia research institute based in Bishkek, shared the belief that tangible progress has been observed most evidently in the economic sphere, underlining transport and transit in particular.
“The development of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route depends on the harmonisation of tariffs and the simplification of customs procedures. In this context, results can be measured by the time and cost involved in transporting goods,” Dzhuraev said.
Dzhuraev further underlined digitalisation as a second promising area, which he defined as the focus of the organisation’s informal summit held in Turkistan in southern Kazakhstan in May.
“The most substantial outcome of the Ankara summit would be the establishment of concrete timelines and mechanisms for implementing decisions already reached – particularly those concerning transport and trade,” he stated.
As part of the OTS Ankara summit, sports is also an area where unity is expected to be shown “in deed.”
During a news conference in Ankara ahead of the summit, Kursad Zorlu, the ruling Justice and Development (AK) Party's deputy chair in charge of relations with Turkic states, said the event includes plans for players from Turkic states to be classified as domestic rather than foreign in one another’s leagues, saying the initiative would foster a football ecosystem across the Turkic world.

Three Swiss brands among world’s 100 most valuable
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:33:18 UTC
17:33:18 KST

Three Swiss brands among world’s 100 most valuable
Three Swiss brands have made it into the world’s top 100 most valuable brands. Zurich Insurance, Nescafé and Nestlé feature in this year’s ranking by the brand consultancy Interbrand.
Zurich Insurance comes out on top, ranking 58th with an estimated brand value of $15 billion (CHF12.42 billion), according to the “Best Global Brands” report published on Thursday. This also makes Zurich the highest-ranked of the four new entrants in this year’s ranking.
The other two Swiss brands are part of the Nestlé Group. Nescafé ranks 70th with a brand value of $12.1 billion. Compared with the previous year, the value of the coffee brand has fallen by 6%. The Nestlé corporate brand ranks 84th with a value of $9.7 billion. Its value remained unchanged year-on-year.
Luxury watchmakers are missing
It is striking that not a single Swiss luxury watchmaker features in the top 100. Well-known brands such as Rolex, Omega, Tag Heuer, Patek Philippe and Audemars Piguet have not made it into the ranking. This is despite the fact that several international luxury brands, such as Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Chanel and Cartier, are represented.
The report does not explain why these Swiss export products – arguably the best known – are missing from the ranking. However, one of the requirements for inclusion is the availability of sufficient publicly accessible financial data. This could pose a particular hurdle for privately owned watch manufacturers.
That said, another Swiss brand could be added in future. The sports footwear manufacturer On is listed by Interbrand among the ten so-called “Brands to Watch”. This watch list features brands that the consultants believe have the potential to rise into the top 100 in future.
Apple remains the most valuable brand
According to Interbrand, the combined value of the top 100 brands has risen by 8.1% to a record total of around $3.9 trillion. The value of 68 brands increased compared with the previous year.
Apple remains at the top with a brand value of around $515 billion. Microsoft follows in second place with just under $444 billion, followed by Google with just over $389 billion.
The remaining places among the ten most valuable brands are occupied by Amazon, Samsung, Nvidia, Instagram, Coca-Cola, Toyota and YouTube.

Drones target one of Russia’s largest chemical complexes in Bashkortostan, media report
This was reported by The Moscow Times, according to Ukrinform.
It is noted that the drones targeted the Bashkir Soda Company (BSC) plant. Smoke began to rise above the plant following the attack.
BSC is one of Russia’s largest chemical complexes and ranks first in the country in the production of soda ash and baking soda.
According to the publication, the enterprise is part of the Roskhim holding company, which holds a controlling stake (57.43%). At the same time, the complex is included in the Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade’s closed registry of defense enterprises.
BSC supplies military plants with hydrochloric acid and dichloroethane, and is also the only Russian producer of terephthaloyl chloride.
This is a critically important compound for the production of synthetic ballistic fibers, high-strength polymers, and aramid materials, according to the report.
It is used to manufacture body armor, helmets, and armor components for military equipment and aircraft.
Prior to this, drones had already attacked the BSC on August 27. Smoke was also seen rising above the facility at that time. Authorities did not comment on the attack.

European Union backtracks on Canada becoming ‘associate member’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:31:09 UTC
17:31:09 KST

European Union backtracks on Canada becoming ‘associate member’
German Chancellor Merz and other EU leaders reportedly pushed for the term to be removed from a joint draft Canada-EU statement.
The European Union has dropped the idea that Canada should become an “associate member” of the bloc, according to media reports.
In a joint draft Canada-EU statement, the terms “associate member” and “associated membership” have been removed, the German news agency dpa and the Reuters news agency reported on Thursday, adding that officials planned to make the statement public on Friday.
The reports come as the EU-Canada summit in Montreal, hosted by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, is expected to start later on Thursday.
In September, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen raised the prospect of Canada becoming the 27-nation EU’s first “associate member”, a striking overture as both seek to pivot away from the United States under President Donald Trump.
However, Reuters and dpa report that von der Leyen’s suggestion of associate membership has been a divisive issue in negotiations among EU countries over the summit declaration, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and several other leaders of fellow member nations pushing for the terms to be removed from the draft, citing diplomats.
The statement now calls for an “ever closer association” between Canada and the EU, and includes a joint initiative to improve international connectivity between Europe, Canada and Asia through “new subsea cable infrastructure”.
It also proposes conducting a joint feasibility study on Canadian liquefied natural gas exports to Europe and enabling young Canadians and Europeans to work across the Atlantic.
Deeper ties to Europe are an important part of Carney’s strategy to reduce Canada’s economic and security reliance on the US since Trump imposed tariffs on Canadian goods. Still, Canada’s efforts to draw closer to the EU risk angering Trump as trade talks between Canada and the US continue.
Trump previously called the EU’s proposal to make Canada an associate member “laughable” and said if he interpreted the move as a “hostile act”, the US might stop trading with Europe “on many things”.
Carney has aimed to deepen ties with the EU, Canada’s second-largest trading partner, since trade relations with the US, Ottawa’s largest economic partner, have been hampered under Trump.
The Canadian leader told reporters on Tuesday that the summit would be the launch of formal negotiations between the EU and Canada that would take another year.
“The good news is it doesn’t matter about specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said. “What matters is the difference it will make to the lives of Canadians.”

China firmly opposes U.S. blacklisting of Chinese firms: commerce ministry
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
16:30:55 CST
17:30:55 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- China strongly condemns and firmly opposes the United States' decision to add three Chinese entities to the so-called "Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List," a spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday.
There is no forced labor in China, and people of all ethnic groups in Xinjiang enjoy freedom and equality in employment, with their labor rights and interests effectively protected by law, the spokesperson said in response to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's announcement that it had added three Chinese entities to the list.
The U.S. measures have no factual basis, the spokesperson said, accusing the U.S. side of persistently manipulating human rights issues to pursue unilateral protectionism and bullying under the guise of human rights protection.
The spokesperson noted that the United States had recently added a large number of Chinese entities to the same list. China had lodged solemn representations with the U.S. side and taken resolute countermeasures.
Disregarding China's firm opposition, the United States has continued to impose new sanctions, this time targeting Chinese biomedical technology companies, the spokesperson said.
Such actions run counter to the consensus reached by the two heads of state, seriously undermine the stability of China-U.S. economic and trade relations, and are contrary to humanitarian principles, the spokesperson added.
The spokesperson urged the United States to immediately stop its political manipulation and smear campaigns, and cease its unjustified suppression of Chinese companies, adding that China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its own interests. ■

WHO Europe Director welcomes Kazakhstan’s plan to increase primary healthcare salaries
Hans Kluge, World Health Organization Regional Director for Europe, has welcomed President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s decision to increase salaries for frontline primary healthcare workers in Kazakhstan by up to 40% starting January 1, 2027, Qazinform News Agency reports.
“I warmly welcome President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s decision to strengthen Kazakhstan’s primary health care workforce,” Kluge said in a statement on X.
More than 77,000 healthcare professionals will benefit from the salary increases, with the size of the raise depending on their length of continuous service.
“Strong primary health care starts with investing in the people who deliver it,” Kluge noted, emphasizing the importance of supporting general practitioners, nurses and other primary healthcare professionals.

One of largest air raids on Moscow, 1,214 UAVs: attacks on Russian regions
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:30:48 UTC
17:30:48 KST

MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Overnight, air defense forces shot down 1,214 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
The attempt by the Ukrainian armed forces to attack Moscow with drones, carried out on Wednesday evening and overnight, was one of the largest of the year so far, according to TASS estimates based on figures published by Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin on his Max channel.
Debris from the UAVs fell on the grounds of a factory in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan. Minor damage was reported, and the plant is operating normally.
TASS has compiled the key details regarding the aftermath.
Scale
- Alert air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 1,214 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles over Russian regions last night, according to the Defense Ministry.
- The ministry reported that enemy UAVs were shot down over the Bryansk, Belgorod, Kursk, Kaluga, Tula, Smolensk, Lipetsk, Voronezh, Tver, Oryol, Ryazan, Vladimir, Samara, Saratov, Penza, and Rostov Regions, the Moscow Region, the Republic of Bashkortostan, and the Republic of Udmurtia.
- An attempted drone attack on Moscow by the Ukrainian armed forces, carried out on Wednesday evening and overnight, was one of the largest of the year so far, according to TASS estimates based on data published by Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin on his Max channel.
- According to the mayor, between 8:30 p.m. Moscow time (5:30 p.m. GMT) on October 28 and 7:00 a.m. Moscow time (4:00 a.m. GMT) on October 29, a total of 613 enemy UAVs were heading toward the Moscow Region.
- Most were neutralized by the Defense Ministry’s air defense forces at a distance, while 231 drones were destroyed on approach to Moscow, he specified.
- Air defense forces destroyed 170 Ukrainian drones over the Kaluga Region, Governor Vladislav Shapsha reported on Max.
- Air defenses destroyed 42 Ukrainian drones over the Tula Region overnight, Governor Dmitry Milyayev wrote on his Max channel.
- A drone attack was thwarted in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan. Eight drones were shot down, Mayor Emil Shaimardanov reported on Telegram.
- Air defense forces destroyed four drones over the Ulyanovsk Region, Governor Alexey Russkikh wrote on his Max channel.
Consequences
- Debris from the UAVs fell on the grounds of a facility in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan, according to a report by Mayor Emil Shaimardanov on Telegram.
- Minor damage was reported.
- The plant is operating normally.
Airport operations
- Russia’s Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsiya) reported that temporary restrictions on aircraft arrivals and departures - necessary to ensure flight safety - had been imposed at Moscow’s Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports.
- These restrictions have now been lifted.
- Two planes flying from Istanbul to Moscow turned back in mid-flight and returned due to safety restrictions at Vnukovo Airport in Moscow, a source in air traffic control services told TASS.
- In addition, restrictions were imposed at airports in Bugulma, Izhevsk, Kazan, Kaluga, Kirov, Nizhnekamsk, Orenburg, Penza, Perm, Samara, Saransk, Saratov, Ulyanovsk, Ufa, Cheboksary, Chelyabinsk, Cherepovets, and Yaroslavl.

Kazakhstan to build nearly 70 new healthcare facilities
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:30:32 UTC
17:30:32 KST

Kazakhstan to build nearly 70 new healthcare facilities
Kazakhstan plans to build nearly 70 new healthcare facilities across the country, Qazinform News Agency quotes Minister of Healthcare Akmaral Alnazarova as saying at a Government's meeting.
According to Alnazarova, the Ministry has begun assessing the need for new healthcare facilities across the country in line with the President's instructions, taking into account regional healthcare needs, demographic trends, and efficiency criteria.
The plans include eight modern perinatal centers with a combined capacity of 1,700 beds in Astana, Almaty, Shymkent, Karaganda, Kaskelen, Kyzylorda, and Oral.
Another seven multidisciplinary children's hospitals, providing a total of 1,550 beds, are planned in Atyrau, Aktobe, Almaty, Shymkent, Kaskelen, Semey, and Aktau.
Astana will also see the construction of a 200-bed pediatric emergency care center and a 350-bed pediatric surgery center.
The projects are designed to expand healthcare services for children and improve access to specialized and advanced medical care nationwide.
Five interregional branches of the National Children's Rehabilitation Center, with a total capacity of 750 beds, are also planned in Almaty, Aktau, Atyrau, Kyzylorda, and Semey.
The plans also include 300-bed multidisciplinary hospitals in East Kazakhstan, Abai, and Turkistan regions, as well as a 325-bed infectious diseases hospital and additional specialized medical facilities in Zhambyl region.
Other planned facilities include 25 outpatient clinics, district hospitals, emergency medical service facilities, blood centers, and specialized healthcare institutions.
Overall, the projects are expected to add or modernize approximately 1.8 million square meters of healthcare infrastructure, expand and upgrade hospital capacity by 9,200 beds, and increase outpatient care capacity by more than 5,300 patient visits per shift.
Earlier, Qazinform News Agency reported that President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev had instructed the Government to raise salaries for primary healthcare workers by up to 40% starting January 1, 2027.

American weightlifter Morris proud of bronze in Chinese debut, eyes bigger prize
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
16:30:21 CST
17:30:21 KST

NINGBO, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- American weightlifter Hampton Morris said he was proud of his bronze medal at the IWF World Championships despite narrowly missing out on gold after failing his final clean-and-jerk attempt.
Morris, 22, lifted 143 kilograms in the snatch and 185kg in the clean and jerk for a total of 328kg, finishing third in the men's 65kg category behind DPR Korea's Pak Myong-jin, who set two world records with a 187kg clean and jerk and a 331kg total, and Türkiye's Muhammed Furkan Ozbek, who took silver with 330kg on Wednesday.
"I'm very, very proud of what I was able to accomplish today. I had some very, very tough competitors," Morris told Xinhua.
There were nevertheless positives for the American, whose 143kg snatch was a personal best, improving on the 142kg he lifted at a domestic competition six weeks earlier.
However, Morris welcomed the challenge posed by his Asian rivals, who had swept the podium at last month's Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.
"Not nervous, but more excited. It's a really incredible opportunity to be able to compete here," he said. "I'm grateful that they're able to push me as much as they have."
The American's respect for his competitors was evident throughout the competition. During his interview with Xinhua, Morris briefly excused himself to greet Chinese lifters Ding Hongjie and He Yueji, shaking hands with both before returning to answer questions.
Competing in China for the first time, Morris has also embraced his experience away from the platform. He shared his amusement at encountering a food-delivery robot at his hotel in Ningbo in a post on Instagram.
"It's amazing. I've really, really enjoyed being here," he said.
Morris is already a familiar figure among Chinese weightlifting fans, having attracted attention for his cheerful demeanor at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he won bronze in the men's 61kg category.
His clean-and-jerk lift of 172kg set an Olympic record and helped him become the first American man to win an Olympic weightlifting medal since 1984.
The lifter from Marietta, Georgia, had previously won clean-and-jerk gold at the 2023 world championships in Riyadh, becoming the first American man to claim a world weightlifting title since 1984.
With a 190kg clean and jerk already achieved in training, Morris believes he has the strength to challenge for further records and titles, with the Los Angeles Games his next major target. ■

The 55-year-old actor, best know for his roles in ER and The Pitt, has officially been named People's 2026 Sexiest Man Alive.
"Doctor, doctor, give me the news / I've got a bad case of loving you..."
After causing countless viewers to swoon in the medical drama ER as Dr. John Carter and making everyone temporarily forget that the American public health care service is one of the most expensive nightmares in the world through his portrayal of Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch in HBO Max's celebrated series The Pitt, Noah Wyle has gone one step further.
The 55-year-old actor, director and producer has officially been named People's 2026 Sexiest Man Alive.
In his People interview, Wyle said he was in disbelief when he got the news.
“I thought that sounded like a prank - just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me,” Wyle said. “I hope this changes everything. I hope it’s just wine and roses, milk and honey from here on out. [Laughs] No, I don’t, but I am going to take a lot of ribbing from friends and family for sure.”
He also shared in the interview that his biggest vice was his Instagram shopping habits, that he hates being late, has an irrational fear of maggots, and has "very, very fast hands".
Before more swooning occurs, he was referring to a secret talent for catching flies. Still impressive.
Wyle's performance in The Pitt has earned him various awards, including this year's Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama, four Primetime Emmy Awards (including Outstanding Lead Actor in 2025 and 2026) and two Writer Guild of America Awards this year.
Season 3 of the medical drama is set to premiere in January 2027.
Launched in 1985 and won that year by Mel Gibson, the Sexiest Man Alive contest marks its 41st year. Wyle succeeds Wicked and Jurassic World Rebirth star Jonathan Bailey, who was the first openly gay man to receive the title last year.
He joins past winners including Patrick Dempsey, Chris Evans, Paul Rudd, Michael B. Jordan, John Legend, Idris Elba, George Clooney and Harrison Ford.
The People edition with Wyle's cover story will be out on 9 November.

Malaysia urges stronger global cooperation for stable natural gas supplies
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
16:30:10 CST
17:30:10 KST

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- Malaysia has called for stronger international cooperation to ensure stable global gas markets and reliable energy supplies, emphasizing that energy security is fundamental to industrial competitiveness, investment confidence and sustainable economic growth, the Ministry of Economy said on Thursday.
As renewable energy deployment accelerates, natural gas will continue to provide the reliability and flexibility needed to support electricity systems and industrial activities, particularly amid rising energy demand across Asia and the ASEAN region, the ministry said in a statement.
Against the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainty, supply disruptions and price volatility, Malaysia emphasized the importance of market transparency, predictable policy frameworks and sustained investment across the natural gas value chain. Greater cooperation between producers and consumers is essential to strengthening supply resilience and maintaining confidence in long-term energy investment, it said.
Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of deepening cooperation through the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and observer countries in market intelligence, liquefied natural gas trade, infrastructure development and technology exchange, the statement said. ■

Over 100 dead after drone strike on market in Sudan's Darfur
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:29:04 UTC
17:29:04 KST

Breadcrumb
Over 100 dead after drone strike on market in Sudan's Darfur
The death toll from an army drone strike on a crowded market in Darfur has risen past 100, residents and a Sudanese rights group said Wednesday, in one of the deadliest single attacks in a conflict increasingly defined by drone warfare.
The strike hit Tanqonj Market on Monday evening in Nyala, the capital of South Darfur and a stronghold of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which has been at war with the army since April 2023.
The city serves as the political and military centre of RSF-controlled territory in Darfur, where the paramilitary group has established an administration rivalling the army-backed, internationally-recognised government in Khartoum.
Nyala has been a frequent target of military strikes since the conflict began.
Witnesses and a medical source initially told AFP the attack killed 21 people and wounded 40 others.
Emergency Lawyers, an NGO which has documented abuses throughout the war, later said the toll stood at 102 with 113 others wounded, including women and children.
"The drone strike turned a civilian marketplace into a scene of mass casualties," the group said, condemning the attack as a "massacre".
'Mass grave'
The market, a bustling hub where residents buy food and other necessities amid wartime shortages, was crowded when the drone struck, according to local residents.
For many families, the scale of the tragedy only became clear as bodies were gathered from the scene and taken for burial.
"I lost my 19-year-old son in Monday's market strike," said Hamdan Suleiman, a resident of Nyala's Doumaya neighbourhood. "We buried him alongside more than 70 bodies in a single site."
A source at Emergency Lawyers told AFP that most of the victims "were buried in a mass grave".
Zahra Hamidan, who sells food at the market, said workers and customers were caught in the blast without warning.
"Next to my food stall," she said, "Halima Issa died along with three girls who worked with her," referring to her co-worker.
As front lines have solidified, both sides have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.
The army has repeatedly targeted RSF positions in Darfur, while the RSF has launched long-range attacks against military and infrastructure sites in army-held areas, including the Khartoum airport, dams and power stations.
According to the United Nations, drone attacks killed more than 300 people and wounded hundreds more during the first three weeks of October alone.
Now in its fourth year, Sudan's conflict has already killed tens of thousands of people, displaced millions and triggered what the UN describes as one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

Spain mourns 68 killed in second deadly high-speed train crash this year
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
08:27:33 UTC
17:27:33 KST

Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 68 people and injured over 100, as relatives sought news of missing loved ones.
The crash occurred on Wednesday morning in Castilla-La Mancha when a state-run Renfe train struck the back of a stationary train operated by private company Iryo.
Emergency crews searched the wreckage overnight near the village of Urda, using cranes to lift mangled metal. Police drones resumed flights over the site at daybreak.
Transport Minister Oscar Puente said an automatic control system had failed along 69 kilometres of track, stopping trains. The control centre later resumed traffic in what he called “inexplicable circumstances”, despite having time to identify and correct the error.
The disaster has raised fresh safety concerns after a January collision in Andalusia killed 46 people when a derailed train crossed onto an adjacent track. That investigation remains ongoing.
Relatives seek answers
A school in Urda, about 130 kilometres south of Madrid, was opened to relatives seeking information about loved ones.
Red Cross workers and psychologists provided support to families, while the Civil Guard established offices in Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to collect DNA samples and help identify victims.
Survivors described the force of the collision and the chaos inside the trains.
Josimar Medina, a 31-year-old Peruvian holidaying in Spain, said he had been asleep when he woke up “in the air”.
Pablo Mejia, 42, said a last-minute seat change had saved his life. He described a powerful impact, passengers piled on top of one another and seats ripped out.
“I think I've been born again,” he told AFP.
Flags flew at half-mast as official ceremonies and public events were cancelled or scaled back.

Elena Teslova
29 October 2026•Update: 29 October 2026
Google’s Russian subsidiary has paid almost 16.8 billion rubles ($207.7 million) in fines imposed in Russia on the US-based Google LLC, the unit’s bankruptcy receiver told a court hearing, Russia's state media reported Thursday.
Valery Talyarovsky, bankruptcy trustee (insolvency administrator) of a Russian branch, said that by Sept. 20, more than 16.7 billion rubles ($206.5 million) had arrived in the bank account of the Russian company, OOO Google, according to state news agency RIA.
About 14.7 billion rubles ($181.7 million) of that amount were written off by Russia’s Federal Bailiffs Service to cover fines against the parent company, he said.
The bailiffs also collected more than 2.1 billion rubles ($26 million) from debtors of the Russian unit under enforcement documents in its favor, and those funds were also used to pay the US corporation’s fines, he said, bringing total payments to almost 16.8 billion rubles ($207.7 million).
Over the course of the bankruptcy proceedings, more than 18.8 billion rubles ($232.5 million) have been paid into the estate of OOO Google, Talyarovsky said.
The remaining funds were used for current claims of the Federal Tax Service and to pay wage arrears to former employees, among other things, he said. More than 400 million rubles ($5 million) went to pay workers.
Google’s debt to Russia for administrative fines reached 2 undecillion rubles and continues to grow due to late payment.
The total fine exceeded the total GDP of the entire world, which was at around $106 trillion in 2023, according to the World Bank.
The figure stems from a dispute that began in 2020 when Google began accumulating daily penalties of 100,000 rubles ($1,000) after losing lawsuits over blocking some Russian YouTube channels, with the penalty doubling each week.
After the beginning of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022, YouTube also blocked other Russian channels, and the number of claimants grew to 17 Russian channels.
In addition, Google has been regularly fined for not complying with Russian legislation.
