Pentagon watchdog refuses to investigate Starlink restrictions for Ukraine – AP
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
03:48:00 EET
10:48:00 KST

Pentagon watchdog refuses to investigate Starlink restrictions for Ukraine – AP
The Pentagon's oversight body, the Office of the Inspector General, has rejected a bipartisan request from US senators to investigate recent disruptions to the Starlink and Starshield services for Ukraine.
Source: Associated Press, citing sources, senators and the Pentagon's response
Details: The AP notes that this raises concerns among American lawmakers that the military and even the independent inspector general are unwilling to challenge the influence that SpaceX head Elon Musk has over the defence communications system.
A bipartisan group of senators asked the Pentagon's watchdog to conduct an investigation after Ukrainian officials reported in October that their connection speeds to the Starlink service and its military version Starshield, both created by Musk, had been restricted.
AP's report emphasises that these services are crucial for ensuring communications in Ukraine during the war, and Ukrainian officials stated that these restrictions hindered the interception of Russian jet attack drones.
In a response obtained by AP, the Pentagon watchdog informed the group of nine lawmakers – four Republicans and five Democrats – that the US Air Force would be better placed to answer their request regarding these concerns.
AP quotes a congressional aide familiar with the situation, speaking on condition of anonymity, who said this is viewed as a refusal by the inspector general to investigate Musk and Starlink, despite being fully capable to do so.
Quote from Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: "It is concerning that the Inspector General has apparently decided not to investigate satellite communication disruptions that Ukraine relies on to protect its civilians."
Details: Shaheen added that "the Trump administration and SpaceX have provided conflicting accounts of what led to those disruptions" and that "there must be an independent accounting and review to determine responsibility and prevent this from happening in the future".
AP adds that the lack of answers raises questions about the extent of influence that Musk, an ally of President Donald Trump, has over this critical communications system.
The congressional aide told the publication that concerns on Capitol Hill regarding Musk's control over Starlink have existed for years and were one of the reasons for creating Starshield, the military version of the system.
When Mollie Halpern, a spokesperson for the Inspector General's Office, was asked about the decision regarding the investigation, she said the watchdog had "carefully considered the congressional request and determined that the matters raised were best addressed by the Department", referring to the Pentagon.
Halpern later added that if new information arises, the Pentagon may revisit its decision.
The Pentagon referred a request for comment to the Inspector General's Office, while the Air Force did not immediately respond to messages requesting comment. Both had previously declined to answer questions regarding the restriction of Ukraine's access to satellite internet.
Background:
- Nine lawmakers asked the Pentagon inspector general to investigate whether any Pentagon or other US government officials had "directed, authorised, approved or had advance knowledge of changes to intelligence-sharing arrangements, warning capabilities, or Starlink and Starshield services affecting Ukraine".
- On 24 October, SpaceX owner Elon Musk commented on restrictions on access to Starlink, claiming that the Ukrainian military had violated the terms of use for this type of communications system. He also said that if Starlink were switched off, "the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately".
- On 21 October, after information about the speed reduction became public, Musk wrote: "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
- Meanwhile, according to The Wall Street Journal, Musk ordered a speed reduction for the military version of Starlink for Ukraine, which rendered a portion of Ukrainian strike drones and interceptor drones practically unusable.
- On 22 October, the WSJ learned that US President Donald Trump had allegedly called Elon Musk and asked him to lift the restrictions on Starshield in Ukraine.
- On 19 October, Zelenskyy said that Starlink and Starshield equipment had stopped working at speeds of 130-161 km/h in various sectors of the front line, disrupting logistics and limiting Ukraine's use of drones.
- Zelenskyy believes that publicity surrounding the connection restrictions has helped to restore the Starlink system's operation to the required speed.

Bloomberg, 2 trading firms agree to pay for faster access to Trump’s Truth Social posts: Sources

Bloomberg, 2 trading firms agree to pay for faster access to Trump’s Truth Social posts: Sources
- Bloomberg, Susquehanna and Jump Trading bought faster access to Trump’s Truth Social posts, paying up to US$100,000 a month for a timing edge that could move markets.
- Trump Media says Truth API is an “industry-standard” product, but critics call it unethical and possibly illegal. Democrats want an SEC probe.
- Intercept Media and the Freedom of the Press Foundation are suing, saying the paid service is “profoundly corrupt” and may block equal access to government information.
AI generated
NEW YORK – Truth Social, the social media platform founded by President Donald Trump, has signed up news and data provider Bloomberg and two Wall Street firms for faster access to the president’s posts, which it sells for up to US$100,000 (S$128,117) a month, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter.
The firms are Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading, both high-frequency trading firms focused on algorithmic and automated strategies.
The service gives subscribers a timing advantage to Trump’s posts on Truth Social, which has the potential to create swings in financial markets and to give Wall Street traders an edge not available to everyday investors.
The companies’ purchase of the Truth API service has not been previously reported. An API is a programming interface that is used as a digital bridge that allows one system to connect to another.
Trump Media and Technology Group announced its fastest-access product in July, and pitched it to trading firms and other financial institutions. The deals likely mark the first time a business tied to a sitting president has sold access to their statements, which some critics have called unethical.
While Truth Social’s pay-for-access plan ventures into untested legal territory, Intercept Media and the Freedom of the Press Foundation sued Trump in August, seeking to block the White House from posting official government announcements exclusively on Truth Social while the paid feed exists.
The suit, which is ongoing, alleges that erecting a financial barrier to government information is potentially unconstitutional and favours wealthy Wall Street firms.
Bloomberg, Jump Trading and Susquehanna declined to comment.
In a statement, Trump Media said: “Truth Social offers an industry-standard API product for which there is significant demand across industries. We take customer confidentiality seriously.
“This reporting is based on misleading information being peddled by anonymous sources aimed at harming our company, customers and shareholders.”
The president’s family trust owns 41% of Trump Media, and Trump is the trust’s sole beneficiary.
Shares of the company have fallen more than 50% so far in 2026.
The market value of Trump Media has been volatile since it went public; it closed at about US$8 billion in its March 2024 debut, but is now worth about $1.8 billion. The company has lost about $1.76 billion since 2024, including non-cash charges.
Trump Media’s Securities and Exchange Commission filings list Trump Jr, as the trustee of the family trust, with sole voting and investment power.
White House spokesman Davis Ingle said neither Trump nor his family is directly involved in any portfolio investment decisions but did not address the allegations that the president was improperly using his office.
Trump Jr did not respond to a comment request. Questions about his role in the business were referred to the Trump Organization, which did not respond to requests for comment.
Market-moving posts
The service is designed to allow customers to read Trump’s posts more quickly than a human would by constantly checking the app.
The timing advantage, described as 50 milliseconds by Trump Media officials, can matter to trading firms or financial news and data organisations because a US president’s posts can create swings in the value of assets.
High-frequency Wall Street traders employ software that ingests news headlines, company announcements and government statements to search for market-moving information. The software can read, analyse and execute a trade in thousandths of a second.
In one example of how Trump’s posts can move markets, oil futures sank after he announced on Truth Social a ceasefire in the Iran war in April.
In August, Trump Media told investors it had “signed more than 10 customer agreements” which Reuters was unable to confirm. The company did not name the clients, but said they were primarily Wall Street trading firms that are paying between US$60,000 and US$100,000 a month.
Reuters, a financial-news competitor to Bloomberg, said in a statement: “We will assess the service, but have no current plans to subscribe.”
Selling faster access to Trump’s posts has drawn criticism from Democrats and media entities.
Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and California’s Adam Schiff said in July that they had asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether the service violated securities laws.
They described it as a “shocking abuse” of office by a president seeking personal gain, without providing further explanation.
The SEC declined to comment.
A TMTG spokesperson said: “Congressional Democrats continue to mischaracterise Truth API either out of ideological opposition to free markets or a failure to grasp the distinction between public and nonpublic information.”
In the lawsuit against Trump by Intercept Media and non-profit Freedom of the Press Foundation, the plaintiffs described the paid data service as “profoundly corrupt”.
The suit also alleges the service would violate the First Amendment rights of the public who do not have equal access to the information and it would violate the Fifth Amendment by charging “unreasonable sums” for equal access to information guaranteed by law.
The White House’s Ingle did not directly address the lawsuit or its allegations, saying: “President Trump only acts in the best interests of the American public – which is why they overwhelmingly re-elected him to this office.” REUTERS

SEOUL, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- Sentiment for South Korean businesses over economic situations rebounded in October, driven by growing production in core industries and booming inbound tourism, central bank data showed Thursday.
The composite business sentiment index (CBSI) in all industries gained 5.1 points from a month earlier to 104.2 in October, turning around from a 0.5-point decline in the previous month, according to the Bank of Korea (BOK).
It marked the highest in over four years since August 2022.
The CBSI among manufacturers advanced 6.1 points to 105.6, fueled by strong production and capital expenditure in primary industries, including semiconductors, automobiles and shipbuilding.
The index for non-manufacturers climbed 4.3 points to 103.2 due to semiconductor-related investments in factories and data centers, alongside soaring inbound tourism during the National Day holiday in China.
The results were based on a survey of 1,941 manufacturers and 1,509 non-manufacturers conducted between Oct. 14 and 21. A reading above the benchmark 100 indicates that optimists outnumbered pessimists.
The economic sentiment index, which reflects sentiment among both businesses and consumers, reached 100.8 in October, up 0.9 points from a month earlier. ■

Feature: From courts to lifestyles, tennis booms across China
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
09:34:30 CST
10:34:30 KST

by Sportswriters Li Chunyu, Li Bowen
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- As 16-year-old home prodigy Sun Xinran clinched the women's singles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Junior Finals in Chengdu on Sunday, Chinese tennis embraced another highlight this autumn besides the ATP and WTA tournaments in the China Swing.
Running through September to November, the China Swing covers cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Wuhan, Chengdu, Hangzhou, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Hong Kong. The 2025 edition drew nearly one million on-site spectators, generating about 250 million yuan (37.5 million U.S. dollars) in ticket revenue and driving over 2.4 billion dollars in related consumption, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
The Tennis Administration Center had already moved to sustain that momentum, issuing reform measures in 2025 covering event supply, talent development and public participation. This September, ahead of the National Day holiday, the General Office of the State Council issued guidelines on unleashing the potential of sports consumption, explicitly supporting high-level professional events such as tennis.
The policy push and the season's momentum have met this autumn. The China Swing has become a window into China's tennis industry and sports-event consumption: from "second-screen" viewing areas to ticket-stub economies, from wild cards tilted toward young Chinese players to a public picking up rackets.
BREAKTHROUGHS AT HOME
Zheng Qinwen's triumph at the China Open was one of the most remarkable moments. The Olympic champion claimed her maiden WTA 1000 title to become the first Chinese player to win the tournament's women's singles crown.
"To play in China is like the fifth Grand Slam for me. I want to perform super well in front of my people," said Zheng, who celebrated her 24th birthday during the China Open in Beijing. "Coming back from the elbow injury, I find my inner fire back and want to be a more aggressive player."
Zheng was not the only Chinese player to benefit from home tournaments. Wild card Sun reached the women's singles last 32 at the China Open, where she faced opponents of rising rank with each round.
"This tournament gave me opportunity to play against top players. From the first round to the third round, my opponents are getting higher in their rankings. This really motivates me to improve myself," said Sun, who took the girls' singles title at this year's US Open.
At the Wuhan Open, qualifier Shi Han upset Alexandra Eala of the Philippines for her first WTA 1000 main-draw win.
Bai Xilin, director of China's Tennis Administration Center, noted that the China Swing provides more opportunities for home players with wild cards and qualifying matches.
"It serves to unleash the potential of our domestic players and inspire their growth in a long run through high-level events," Bai said.
For overseas athletes, the China Swing offers a chance to explore the host cities. Novak Djokovic took the Summer Palace as a favorite destination.
"I respect Chinese culture and tradition very much. Actually I was staying in a hotel that is just next to the Summer Palace. I've been going there every day. No joke. It's a stunning place more than just nature," said the 39-year-old Djokovic, who claimed his seventh China Open men's singles title this year.
"Tennis brings together players and fans from different countries and backgrounds. Through the tournament coverage and the players' own social channels, international audiences can also discover more aspects of China," said Fabrice Chouquet, a WTA senior official.
ECONOMIC ACES
For Vietnamese businessman Dang Phu, his destination in China has always been the Canton Fair in autumn. But this year, he and colleagues arrived earlier than usual to watch the Wuhan Open and then the Shanghai Masters.
"We wanted to see top players compete in person and experience the atmosphere," Dang said.
"People came to watch the match not only for the competition itself, but to feel the urban life. So, the organizers need to focus more on how an event can draw larger crowds and channel these visitors into a full range of consumption scenarios across the host city," said Huang Haiyan, a professor at Beijing Sport University.
According to the China Open organizing committee, total consumption during the tournament is projected to exceed 8.2 million dollars, up 55 percent year-on-year, with licensed product revenue doubling to 4.2 million dollars. Over 450,000 visitors entered the National Tennis Center, up 25 percent, including around 60 percent from other cities and nearly 10,000 international spectators.
Even though the Wuhan Open was not scheduled for the National Day holiday this year and home favorite Zheng was absent through injury, the tournament still drew 202,700 on-site spectators, 48 percent of whom traveled from other cities.
"The tournament not only drives direct spending on tickets, licensed products and catering services, but also spurs consumption on accommodation, transport and tourism," said Hong Xuyan, deputy director of the Wuhan Sports Bureau.
At the Shanghai Masters, around 248,000 on-site spectators watched the tournament, two thirds from outside Shanghai. "The total revenue reached 75 million dollars, with sponsorship contributing roughly 50 percent and ticketing for 20 percent," said Yang Yibin, chairman of Shanghai Juss Sports Development Group.
"Tennis fans feature high per-capita spending. They stay longer and always follow a complete consumption chain spanning tickets, catering, accommodation and tourism for multiplier effect," noted Wang Xueli, a professor at Tsinghua University's School of Economics and Management.
The broader industry is growing too. China's tennis industry was worth 5.5 billion dollars in 2024, up 15 percent year-on-year, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
NURTURING TENNIS CULTURE
Chinese tennis player Ji Mianyi, 20, sensed the tennis boom through her family and friends.
"When the topic turns to sports, they used to think of table tennis or badminton first. But after Zheng won the women's singles gold at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, more people around me wanted to learn from scratch and asked me how long it takes to be able to compete," Ji said.
Her observations are borne out by the data. China's tennis population reached 25.19 million in 2024, up 28.03 percent from 19.67 million in 2021 and about a quarter of the global total, according to the Tennis Administration Center. The number of courts rose from 49,767 to 53,805 over the same period, up 8.12 percent.
Two decades ago, when Zheng Jie and Yan Zi claimed China's first women's doubles Grand Slam title at the 2006 Australian Open, tennis still seemed far from most Chinese people. The country had nearly two million participants and about 10,000 courts, according to figures from that year.
"There were much fewer youth tennis tournaments in China at that time," Zheng Jie recalled. "Then, the outstanding performance of Chinese players, including Li Na and Zheng Qinwen, kept stoking public enthusiasm for tennis."
By 2025, Guangdong, Sichuan, Hubei, Beijing and Zhejiang are the top five regions by tennis population, all hosting ATP or WTA tournaments as part of the China Swing. Only 5,402 youth players are registered with the General Administration of Sport, but roughly 506,000 young players have competition records outside the registered system, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
Shanghai, home to the Masters, has maintained strong momentum. At the PMAX Tennis Center, its 12 courts have become a thriving hub.
"Our tennis center hosts training courses and tournaments, catering to enthusiasts of different stages," introduced Jia Jingzhe, one of the center's partners. "Powered by this model, the center's monthly revenue has been around 200,000 dollars since March this year, more than quadrupling over four years compared with 2022."
Among the customers at PMAX, adults account for more than 60 percent, with women in the majority. According to the Shanghai Tennis Association, the city's tennis-playing population reached 980,000 in 2025, and more than 30 newly opened venues added over 100 standard courts.
"Tennis is an integral part of my life," said enthusiast Zhu Lingjun, who plays three to four hours every week and uses AI to review her game.
From professional tournaments to grassroots courts, tennis has been evolving into a lifestyle in China.
"International studies have found that long-term tennis participation can help extend people's lifespan by improving sleep and modulating nervous system," Bai said. "Our goal is to ensure that tennis is accessible to everyone, and we are striving toward that vision." ■

5 Things to Consider When Planning Interior Thresholds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:30:00 UTC
10:30:00 KST

An opening between two rooms shapes how people move through a building, what they see from one space to another, and whether an area feels connected or separate. Although doors are among the most frequently used interior architectural elements, their impact on the interior organization is often considered late in the design process. Yet their movement and relationship to surrounding surfaces influence circulation, furniture placement, and the perception of space.
In residential renovations, these decisions are particularly important. Existing walls, structural elements, building services, and ceiling heights can limit options, while new layouts often balance open-plan living with the need for privacy. In new construction, architects have greater freedom to coordinate wall cavities, suspended ceilings, and door mechanisms from the outset.
The question is how two spaces should relate: remain connected, be separated, or alternate between the two? Openings, partitions, hinged doors, pivot doors, sliding doors, and furniture each offer different possibilities. Door systems such as those developed by ECLISSE provide different approaches to these transitions, responding to existing construction conditions and the intended spatial arrangement.
1. Defining the Relationship Between Spaces
A kitchen connected to a living room may benefit from a wide opening that preserves visual continuity while still allowing separation during cooking or entertaining. A home office may stay open during the day but still need visual and acoustic privacy for focused work or calls. In both cases, the design must balance openness with the option of separation.
Not every transition requires a door. Changes in floor finish, deeper openings, screens, or variations in ceiling height can distinguish areas without closing them off. Furniture can serve a similar purpose: a kitchen island, freestanding storage unit, or shelving system can define zones, guide circulation, and provide storage without creating a full-height partition.
2. Choosing a Door System
The door mechanism affects circulation and usable space. Hinged doors require clearance for their swing, which must be coordinated with furniture, corridors, and adjacent doors. Pivot doors let larger panels rotate around pivot points set away from a conventional side hinge.
Sliding doors move parallel to a wall or partition, avoiding the floor space a swinging panel requires. Ceiling-, surface-mounted, and integrated sliding door systems such as the ECLISSE Exo and Endo leave the panel visible when open, while pocket doors slide into a cavity within the wall. The latter leave the opening unobstructed and free up the adjacent wall surface, but require sufficient space within the partition and coordination with electrical installations and other services.
The distinction becomes particularly relevant in renovations. A ceiling- or surface-mounted track can be installed without creating a door cavity within the wall or requiring a suspended ceiling, which can simplify projects where existing construction must remain in place. A ceiling-integrated sliding door and pocket door may be easier to accommodate in a new partition designed around the mechanism. The decision depends on available construction depth, the intended opening, and the functions the surrounding wall must support.
3. Visible or Concealed
For sliding doors, the sliding mechanism is part of the architectural detail. Its position affects the ceiling, wall finish, and the opening's appearance when the panel is open or closed. Choosing between a visible track and a recessed system also influences how the door relates to surrounding surfaces.
In a ceiling- or surface-mounted sliding door system, such as the ECLISSE Exo, a track support is mounted on the wall or ceiling and concealed behind a 65-mm-high aluminum pelmet. Its appearance can coordinate with the surrounding surfaces or remain a visible architectural detail, available in finishes such as white, black, or a paintable primer.
A ceiling-integrated sliding door system, such as ECLISSE Endo, integrates the track support into a suspended ceiling. Once finished, the support sits flush with the ceiling, leaving only a slim slot for the visible sliding guide. The primer-coated surface can be painted to match the ceiling, allowing the mechanism to recede visually. The system can be installed in front of or inside the passageway, ideal for large openings. This approach requires the ceiling construction to accommodate the recessed support; however, it is adjustable and can accommodate unevenness in the ceiling slab. Both systems accommodate wooden panels and glass panels with aluminum frames. Individual panels can measure up to 1,300 mm wide and 3 m high, with a specified thickness of 40 mm.
4. Configuring Openings
The passage width affects the number of panels and the space needed for their movement. A single panel may suit a standard doorway, while wider openings can use two opposing panels that meet in the center. Multiple tracks accommodate several panels, and fixed panels can extend the overall glazed or opaque surface.
Sliding door systems, such as ECLISSE Exo and Endo, are available in single-, double-, and triple-track configurations. Both also allow two opposing panels on the same track, with fixed panels as an additional option. These arrangements can accommodate wider connections between living areas, kitchens, and multipurpose rooms. The open position requires as much consideration as the closed one. Available wall or ceiling length, where panels collect, and the position of switches and furniture all affect how much of the passage remains clear.
5. The Door as Part of the Interior
Material choices also affect the relationship between spaces. A door's finish influences how the threshold reads within a room. A panel matching the wall color can reduce visual interruptions, while contrasting timber, glass, or a dark track can emphasize the opening. Glass maintains visual continuity, while an opaque panel provides greater visual separation. A sliding panel can close off an area when needed and leave the layout open when retracted. Flush-to-wall doors offer another way to maintain continuity by aligning the door leaf with the surrounding wall.
The aim is not to make every boundary disappear, but to determine where it should remain visible, where it should recede, and how it should respond to everyday use. Coordinating the opening, panel movement, supporting structure, and finish allows doors to become part of the spatial plan.

Over 135,000 displaced in Yemen’s Taiz province in 2 months: Minister
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:24:38 UTC
10:24:38 KST

Shukri Hussein and Tarek Chouiref
29 October 2026•Update: 29 October 2026
 
More than 135,000 people were displaced in Yemen’s southwestern Taiz province over a roughly two-month period, a minister said Wednesday, citing government figures that also recorded 79 civilian deaths and 206 injuries.
Social Affairs and Labor Minister Mukhtar Omar Saleh Al-Yafei presented the figures at a government news conference in the temporary capital Aden, according to Yemen’s SABA news agency.
The figures cover Aug. 10 to Oct. 15, a period of military escalation and a siege that the government accuses the Houthi group of imposing on parts of the province.
Al-Yafei said field monitoring recorded the displacement of 19,600 families comprising 135,587 people, including 52,979 children.
The ministry documented 494 violations against civilians during the same period, including the killings and injuries. Damage was reported to 56 residential buildings, 12 educational facilities, eight health facilities and 10 roads and bridges, along with other property and public services.
The minister called for a broader humanitarian response to address funding shortfalls and gaps in essential services.
Taiz Governor Nabil Shamsan said more than 1.3 million people lived in six districts affected by the siege, while shelling had damaged or destroyed about 676 homes.
He warned that services at 12 hospitals and 18 health centers were under threat. In Houthi-controlled districts, 120 health facilities had stopped operating entirely and another 66 were only partially functioning, disrupting care for more than 186,000 children under five and nearly 23,000 pregnant women.
Taiz, Yemen’s most populous province, remains divided between government forces and the Houthis. Government forces control Taiz city, the provincial capital, and other parts of the province.
Since July, a military escalation between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis has resumed, particularly in Taiz and Lahj, killing and injuring thousands, according to UN reports.
Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014. A Saudi-led Arab coalition intervened in March 2015 in support of Yemen’s internationally recognized government.

US fiscal pressures to persist regardless of midterm election outcome: Fitch
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:19:49 UTC
10:19:49 KST

Diyar Güldoğan
29 October 2026•Update: 29 October 2026
 The US is likely to face continued fiscal pressures regardless of the outcome of the upcoming midterm elections, with rising entitlement spending and debt-servicing costs threatening to push government debt higher, Fitch Ratings said Wednesday.
In a report, the credit rating agency warned that Democratic control of one or both chambers of Congress could increase the likelihood of political brinkmanship over the federal debt ceiling and government funding, potentially putting further pressure on the country's already-large fiscal deficit.
However, Fitch said the underlying drivers of the US fiscal outlook would persist regardless of which party controls Congress, pointing to rising entitlement expenditures and debt-servicing costs as key challenges.
Without policy changes, these structural pressures are likely to lead to a further deterioration in the country's debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio, the agency said.
The US federal budget deficit reached nearly $2 trillion, equivalent to 6.1% of GDP, in fiscal 2026, according to Fitch.
The agency forecasts that the general government deficit, which includes the balances of state and local governments, will widen to 7.5% of GDP in 2026 and 7.6% in 2027. State and local government balances account for around 1% of GDP.
Such a deficit would be the highest among sovereigns rated in the 'AA' category, Fitch said.
The agency also warned that the fiscal priorities of both major political parties could add to budgetary pressures unless offset by other measures.

Oleshky Truce Enters Third Day As Humanitarian Hopes Collide With Russia Deportation Fears
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:17:39 UTC
10:17:39 KST

A Russian attack on Ukraine's eastern city of Dnipro killed at least 14 people and injured 14 others, according to Ukrainian officials, as a fragile cease-fire around Russian-occupied Oleshky entered its third day on October 29.
Russian forces struck a railway station platform in Dnipro with a jet-powered drone, near a train bound for Zaporizhzhya, according to Ukraine's national railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsya.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack "horrific," saying that Russian forces had "launched a drone attack on a platform where an ordinary commuter train and a scheduled passenger train were standing."
"How many terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on certain Russian oligarchs and the Russian energy sector, rather than de-escalating?” he added.
"This is a genocidal war," Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov wrote following the attack.
The attack in Dnipro came as a cease-fire in Oleshky continued for more than 50 hours, with both Russian and Ukrainian delegations heading to the city in southern Ukraine, according to officials in Kyiv and Moscow.
The localized truce, brokered with the involvement of US first lady Melania Trump, took effect on October 27 and is scheduled to last until November 1. Ukrainian and US officials told RFE/RL that no violations had been reported during its first two days.
Still, the absence of reported breaches has done little to resolve concerns over the operation’s consequences. Ukrainian officials and humanitarian advocates say its success will depend on whether residents receive aid, can evacuate safely, and are free to choose their destinations.
The cease-fire comes as Washington and Moscow prepare for a possible diplomatic encounter and US lawmakers debate further support for Ukraine.
Lawmakers Warn Of Forced Deportations
The bipartisan Congressional Ukraine Caucus welcomed the cease-fire on October 28, crediting Melania Trump's efforts while raising alarm over reports that Russian authorities were preventing Oleshky residents from evacuating to Ukrainian-controlled territory.
In a statement shared with RFE/RL, caucus co-chairs -- Democratic Representatives Marcy Kaptur of Ohio and Mike Quigley of Illinois, and Republican Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania and Joe Wilson of South Carolina -- called for safe evacuation, humanitarian assistance, and the freedom to reunite with loved ones.
“Forcibly transferring or deporting civilians from occupied territory is a war crime,” the lawmakers said, urging Russia to end coercive practices and let residents choose where to go.
They warned that Moscow must not turn the cease-fire into another instrument of repression after residents endured severe deprivation and the threat of relentless drone attacks. The statement also cited Russia’s broader record of alleged abuses against Ukrainians, including the abduction of tens of thousands of children.
Oleshky, across the Dnieper River from Kherson, has been under Russian occupation since 2022. The US-based advocacy organization Razom for Ukraine estimates that 1,700 to 2,000 civilians remain trapped there, including about 50 children. Many are elderly people, people with disabilities, and their caregivers.
Residents face acute shortages of food and medicine and lack reliable access to drinking water, electricity, gas, and heating. Regular road deliveries of food stopped in May, according to Razom. Mines, drone attacks, and damaged infrastructure have made escape perilous, while Ukrainian officials and advocates accuse Russian forces of obstructing departures and aid deliveries.
Relief Effort Faces Scrutiny
Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said preparations for the humanitarian mission were continuing under an agreement with Russia. Working with Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova, he has coordinated the effort through arrangements facilitated by Melania Trump.
After briefing Ukrainian lawmakers on October 28, Lubinets thanked the US first lady for her involvement, saying the priority was to implement the agreement, help civilians, and save lives.
Melania Trump said Russia and Ukraine had begun demining operations to create safe passage for humanitarian assistance. She later announced that four Newsmax journalists would travel to Oleshky to document the operation alongside Russian and Ukrainian humanitarian representatives.
But advocates say journalists alone cannot substitute for independent monitors able to verify consent and investigate alleged abuses. Daniel Balson, Razom’s director of advocacy, told RFE/RL that Melania Trump’s efforts deserved recognition but warned that the lack of credible third-party monitoring was a serious weakness.
“There has been no provision for credible third party monitors from the ICRC or the UN to oversee their evacuation,” he said, referring to the International Committee of the Red Cross and the United Nations.
Balson warned that Russian President Vladimir Putin could use the operation to forcibly deport nearly 2,000 civilians, including children.
The Institute for the Study of War said on October 28 that it remained unclear how Russian authorities would treat evacuees or whether residents would have a genuine, uncoerced choice to return to Ukrainian-controlled territory.
Razom warned that people transferred to Russian-controlled territory could face interrogation, filtration procedures, detention, or pressure to obtain Russian documents. Children could be separated from relatives or placed in Russian custody.
The organization also cautioned that Moscow might use images of evacuees to suggest Ukrainians were willingly choosing to move to Russia.
Yuriy Boyechko, chief executive of the US-based humanitarian organization Hope for Ukraine, raised a separate concern, telling RFE/RL that the cease-fire risked becoming a tool for both forced population transfers and Russian military repositioning.
He alleged that Russian forces were preventing civilians from evacuating to Ukrainian-controlled territory across the Dnieper River and instead directing them toward occupied Crimea or Russia.
Boyechko said Russian troops were moving heavy armor, artillery, and fresh units toward the riverbanks, using the pause to rotate frontline forces and establish forward positions.
“Under the guise of a temporary truce, Russian units are transferring heavy armor, artillery, and fresh battle groups toward the riverbanks,” he said, warning that the movements could signal preparations for a renewed offensive intended to pressure and potentially retake Kherson.
Lavrov’s Atlanta Visit Raises Diplomatic Stakes
The cease-fire’s uncertain prospects come as Washington and Moscow face a new opportunity for diplomatic contact. Moscow confirmed on October 28 that Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov would lead Russia’s delegation to a G20 foreign ministers meeting in Atlanta on October 30-31. The United States holds the group’s rotating presidency this year.
Lavrov’s attendance puts him in the same city as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, creating an opportunity for direct contact, though diplomatic sources told RFE/RL that no meeting between them had been confirmed.
Republican Representative Don Bacon criticized the prospect of Lavrov attending, telling RFE/RL that Russian leaders should not be welcomed at international forums while Moscow continues its war against Ukraine.
“As long as Putin is waging war against Ukraine and bombing cities, Russian leaders should not be welcomed in any of these forums,” Bacon said. “They lead a pariah state.”
Lavrov’s visit announcement came a day after he dismissed a diplomatic outreach to Putin by Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store as offering nothing new. He also warned that the information war surrounding Ukraine would continue and likely intensify.
Zelenskyy welcomed the Nordic leaders’ efforts, as Kyiv seeks to ensure Ukraine’s interests remain central to any negotiations.
Kyiv Seeks Leverage Ahead Of Planned Talks
Zelenskyy is also coordinating with European partners ahead of planned negotiations. After meeting Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten on October 28, he said preparations were continuing for a planned trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi, and that he and Jetten discussed how European partners could ensure their interests were taken into account.
Ukraine has argued that negotiations are unlikely to produce a durable settlement if Moscow believes it can secure further gains through military pressure.
In Washington, a bipartisan group of lawmakers in the House of Representatives is backing legislation to address obstacles to transfers of US-origin weapons to Ukraine through third countries.
Democrats Bill Keating, Sarah McBride, and Gregory Meeks, and Republicans Joe Wilson, Don Bacon, and Brian Fitzpatrick have introduced a bill called Fast Tracking European Investment in Ukraine’s Defense Act, which would amend US arms-export law to address third-party transfers of certain defense articles to Kyiv.
Diesel Deal Fuels Another Washington Dispute
A separate dispute over Russian energy imports has exposed further divisions in US policy toward Moscow.
Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal urged the shipping company behind the Malta-flagged tanker Agioi Fanendes to turn back before delivering a reported 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel to New York. The vessel reportedly loaded its cargo at Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22 and is expected to arrive on November 7.
Blumenthal argued that the shipment could violate the 2022 law prohibiting imports of Russian oil and petroleum products. He said President Donald Trump’s recently announced deal to secure Russian diesel supplies could not override restrictions enacted by Congress.
“The president may have given a license to facilitate this transaction, but only Congress can make it legally valid,” Blumenthal wrote in a letter to the shipping company’s managing director.
The deal, announced on October 9 with the stated aim of easing fuel prices, has drawn criticism from lawmakers who say Russian energy purchases could provide Moscow with additional revenue to finance its war. Meeks has introduced legislation seeking to block Russian diesel imports and impose further sanctions.

Website reporting on crime in Victoria staffed by workers in Philippines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:16:44 UTC
10:16:44 KST

News website reporting on crime in Victoria staffed by workers in Philippines
In short:
The director of a home security business has admitted to paying people in the Philippines to create stories about crime in Victoria for a news website he owns.
The stories on Victoria Crime News are credited to a fictional team of local Australian reporters.
The website has been recommended by AI chatbots as a reliable source of news despite some articles containing glaring errors.
The director of a website that reports news stories on Victorian crime has admitted its local team of reporters does not exist and that he uses workers in the Philippines.
Victoria Crime News (VCN) credits its stories to a four-person team of specialist crime reporters who have filed over 250 articles since February 2026.
But when ABC NEWS Verify spoke to its owner, Craig Winder, he admitted his team was not local at all.
"I have a team of writers over in the Philippines … I just tell them to not write anything incriminating."
The site features stories containing glaring errors and AI-generated photos.
Tests conducted by ABC NEWS Verify of prominent chatbots have found it is being recommended as a reliable source of information by Google's Gemini and X's Grok.
'Pink slime' journalism
The site is an example of so-called "pink slime" journalism, according to Momoko Fujita, a senior lecturer at the University of Canberra, who researches how digital platforms and media influence people's behaviour.
Pink slime refers to websites that purport to publish legitimate news but instead publish AI-enhanced content for the purpose of influencing audiences or generating revenue.
"If it's not fake, then why would they put fake names?" she said.
VCN claims its "editorial team may use generative-AI tools as part of research, headline drafting or copy editing", but assures readers that every article is written by a "named human reporter".
Over the phone, Mr Winder provided more detail on the VCN's human reporters, saying he actually employed a roster of workers based in the Philippines who filed stories attributed to fictitious reporters with "Aussie names" listed on the website's editorial team.
Mr Winder said he had "changed a lot of staff over the last three years" owing to resignations or poor performance.
When pressed by ABC NEWS Verify whether it was deceptive to use fake bios for his Philippines journalists, he said: "I suppose it is a bit deceptive, to be honest, just to be black and white."
Mr Winder told ABC NEWS Verify he set up the website to raise awareness of crime in his state and compel the government to "do more" to combat crime.
He is also the director of a company specialising in home security installations.
Mr Winder said he has been a victim of several attempted burglaries which partly motivated him to create a news website focusing on reporting crime in his state.
AI images and false details
Some of the news stories are factually incorrect or show indications of being AI-enhanced rewrites of stories first published by news outlets such as The Age and ABC News.
This includes the use of near-identical passages and VCN's inclusion of AI-generated images for some stories.
Some AI-generated images accompanying stories show little resemblance to the locations they purport to show.
A VCN image accompanying a story on the firebombing of a grocer in Melbourne's Deer Park, for instance, shows little resemblance to the actual shopfront, which was photographed following the blaze as part of the ABC's reporting.
A handful of stories are also accompanied by images that appear to have no relevance whatsoever.
The image used in this article bears no relationship to its subject. (Supplied: Victoria Crime News)
Other stories contain glaring factual errors.
VCN's story on the cold case homicide of Kade Hall claims Mr Hall was "last seen in 2014".
Details openly available on the Victoria Police website state that Mr Hall was last seen in 2002 when his body, which had sustained fatal gunshot wounds, was found in bushland near Kalorama in Victoria.
Other cold cases featured on the VCN website contain significant factual errors, such as the murder of Shannon McCormack, a man who was fatally assaulted in Melbourne's CBD in 2002 by an unknown assailant.
His case on the VCN website describes him as a female who was last seen in the early 2000s before mysteriously disappearing.
Mr Winder said he was surprised to learn about inaccuracies in articles on his website, telling ABC NEWS Verify that he would raise it with his team in the Philippines and correct any inaccuracies.
He said it was not his intention for the website to plagiarise original reporting by real reporters.
"I never want to take away from proper, true journalism and journalists, and I never want to take their information research away from them," he said.
Former police domain used for pink slime
The site's domain address was previously operated by the Victorian Police Force, which used it to publish official police announcements until 2019.
How the domain looked when it was run by Victoria Police in 2019. (Supplied: Victoria Police)
It was later acquired by Mr Winder, who used the domain to launch VCN, which started publishing stories in February 2026.
Dr Fujita agreed it was concerning the site was being recommended by AI chatbots, but she was unsurprised.
"[The chatbots] recommended this as a reliable source because … search engines use AI today.
"The way this website is structured, and the kind of keywords they use, is optimised for AI search engines."
She added the website's selective editorial focus "suggests there is [a] certain agenda behind this operation".

On November 4, Julia’s great-grandniece, Maria Juncal, the sixth generation of the Borull family of flamenco dancers and musicians, will bring her inherited talent to Tel Aviv a full 100 years after her great-great-grandfather’s passing.
She will share her dancing, interpreted and enriched but still flamenco in its purest form, with lovers of the genre and of Spanish and Latin music and dance in general.
Juncal has her regular local fans, as she has been visiting Israel for years, sharing performances that come from the heart, regale, and enchant.
Despite the war with Iran, she performed in Tel Aviv last year – as always, under the auspices of Silvia Baro Productions and the Suzanne Dellal Center. This year, since the venue is being renovated, her show will take place at the Arison Center.
Since 2021, she has been based in Mexico City, where she opened a tablao flamenco (flamenco review), and she performs worldwide.
Four local flamenco musicians to join Juncal

Leak website releases data on tens of thousands of DHS employees

01:16:33 UTC
10:16:33 KST

The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.
DHS said in a statement it was "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." The agency said it was working to ensure its employees were properly protected and would update the public "when more information is available.”
The disclosure, which the nonprofit data transparency group says draws on information obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace," is the third major government data leak to make headlines in the past month.
In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the Defense Department was hit with a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.
The DHS data includes names, phone numbers, and email addresses of employees from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and other DHS component agencies.
Also included in the data were job titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics, and undercover work.
In a statement, Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder Emma Best said the hacktivist known as "maia arson crimew" developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would "replace anonymity with accountability" and empower journalists, guide public records requests, and boost congressional oversight.
The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data it said that DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs" and that it hoped the data "can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction."
Entity claimed responsibility for previous DHS hack
The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.
Best's statement said the Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query, "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised."
Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove, but it was able to match personal information about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs.
Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.
In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees' LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.

Israel's underworld at the ballot box: Who are crime figures backing?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:15:51 UTC
10:15:51 KST

Associates of some of Israel's most prominent organized crime figures revealed their political preferences on Wednesday, including support for Israel's two main Arab parties, Ra’am and the Joint List, as well as left-wing politician Yair Golan, Walla learned from sources close to the figures.
Throughout the year, they keep the police, the State Attorney's Office, and the courts busy. Yet on election day, even well-known figures from Israel's criminal underworld turn their attention to the question occupying the country: Who will sit in the next Knesset?
Behind the names associated with organized crime syndicates lie political preferences, and not all of them are predictable. Some are particularly surprising.
In conversations with Walla on Wednesday, associates of figures linked to the criminal underworld revealed where their political sympathies lie.
Sources close to the Jarushi family, associated with one of Israel's most prominent crime organizations, indicated support for Ra'am and the Joint List.
Perhaps even more intriguing is Eitan Hiya's political preference. According to his associates, he favors Yair Golan, one of the most prominent figures on the Israeli political Left.
This political alignment may not be expected, but it sheds light on the complex range of political preferences within the criminal underworld.
There is no single, unified political camp or shared position. Moreover, affiliation with a particular crime organization or family does not necessarily mean its members vote the same way.
It is important to note that the information about these political preferences comes from associates of the individuals involved and does not verify the ballots they actually cast.
There is an interesting paradox at the heart of this story. On the one hand, law enforcement authorities combat criminal organizations and seek to restrict their activities. On the other, individuals associated with these organizations, provided they retain the right to vote, can participate in the democratic process and influence the composition of the Knesset.
That same Knesset is responsible, among other things, for determining the legal tools available to the state in its fight against organized crime.
Nearly 89% voter turnout among eligible prisoners
Voting also took place in Israel's prisons on Wednesday.
Polling stations at all detention facilities closed at 8 p.m., with the Israel Prison Service (IPS) reporting an 88.7% voter turnout among eligible prisoners and detainees.
According to figures from the IPS Operations Division, voting was coordinated with the Central Elections Committee following operational preparations led by IPS Commissioner Kobi Yaakobi.
Judges and official observers visited detention facilities throughout the day, while voting was conducted by secret ballot under strict security and public order measures.
The voting took place against the backdrop of the state's ongoing struggle against organized crime.
The Law for the Protection of the Public from Criminal Organizations, which came into effect at the end of 2024, allows courts to impose restrictions on individuals operating within criminal organizations, even without a formal indictment, provided the strict legal conditions are met.
Among other measures, courts may order individuals to stay away from certain areas, confine them to their homes, prohibit contact with specified individuals, and impose additional restrictions.
The law gives law enforcement authorities tools to prevent serious harm to public safety, including in circumstances where that objective cannot be achieved through criminal proceedings, while seeking to minimize infringements on individual rights.
Yet there is one right that association with the criminal underworld does not, in itself, take away: the right to vote.
While the state seeks to keep criminal organizations away from centers of power, a ballot cast by someone associated with such groups carries exactly the same weight as that of any other eligible citizen.
That is perhaps the great irony of election day.
The police may monitor criminal organizations, the State Attorney's Office may seek to restrict their activities, and the courts may issue orders against their members. But behind the voting booth curtain, as long as the right to vote remains intact, there is no distinction between the investigator and the person under investigation.
Both cast their ballots for the same Knesset.

What is celebrated on October 29 in Ukraine and around the world
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
03:14:48 EET
10:14:48 KST

What is celebrated on October 29 in Ukraine and around the world
Kyiv • UNN
October 29 marks World Stroke Day, World Psoriasis Day, Financial Independence Day, and World Ultrasound Day. The faithful honor Anastasia of Rome.
On October 29, the world observes World Stroke Day and World Psoriasis Day under the auspices of international medical organizations. According to the new-style church calendar, Saint Anastasia the Roman, a venerable martyr, is commemorated, while according to the old style, Saint Longinus the Centurion, who stood by the Lord’s Cross, is remembered, UNN reports.
World Stroke Day
The date was established by the World Stroke Organization in 2006. The event is intended to draw public attention to cerebrovascular diseases, which are among the leading causes of disability and death worldwide. The day emphasizes the importance of prevention (controlling blood pressure, quitting smoking, and eating a healthy diet) and raising public awareness of the first symptoms of stroke using the BRAIN/FAST acronym, when timely assistance within the “golden window” of 4.5 hours can minimize severe consequences for the brain.
World Psoriasis Day
Established in 2004 at the initiative of the International Federation of Psoriasis Associations and officially supported by the World Health Organization. The medical observance aims to raise awareness of psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis—chronic autoimmune diseases affecting more than 125 million people worldwide. The event calls for overcoming the stigmatization and social isolation of patients, expanding access to modern biological medicines, and providing comprehensive psychological and dermatological care.
International Financial Independence Day
A popular international observance dedicated to promoting financial literacy, personal budget planning, and investment culture. The observance encourages people to build financial safety nets, optimize debt obligations, develop passive sources of income, and achieve personal material freedom from daily economic instability.
World Ultrasound Day
A professional and scientific observance for ultrasound diagnostics specialists, recognizing the revolutionary contribution of ultrasound technologies to medicine, industry, and scientific research. In healthcare, ultrasound is one of the safest, most accessible, and most highly informative methods for imaging organs, blood vessels, and fetal development during pregnancy.
According to the new calendar, Orthodox and Greek Catholic believers commemorate Saint Anastasia the Roman, a venerable martyr—a Christian maiden who was raised in a monastery near Rome. During the persecution under Emperor Decius, she openly professed her faith in Christ before the governor Probus, endured brutal torture, and accepted a martyr’s death by beheading.
According to the old calendar, believers commemorate Saint Longinus the Centurion —a Roman centurion who stood guard by the Lord’s Cross on Golgotha and witnessed the crucifixion and subsequent Resurrection of Christ. Having seen the miracles, Longinus believed in the Savior, refused the bribe offered by the Jewish elders, left military service, and set out to preach the Gospel in his homeland of Cappadocia, where he was later executed on the orders of Pontius Pilate.

Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:13:05 UTC
10:13:05 KST

Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
- Date:
- October 28, 2026
- Source:
- Science China Press
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered that magma deep inside Earth can store surprising amounts of extra oxygen, potentially revealing a hidden contributor to our planet's oxygen-rich atmosphere. The findings suggest that ancient volcanic eruptions may have helped transform Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago, with implications for understanding life on other planets.
- Share:
Scientists have discovered that molten rock deep inside Earth can store far more oxygen than previously believed. The finding challenges long-standing assumptions about magma and raises an intriguing possibility: oxygen released from Earth's interior may have helped transform the planet's atmosphere billions of years ago.
Through high-pressure experiments and advanced computer simulations, researchers found that magma can absorb additional oxygen beyond the amount normally required by its chemical composition. This hidden oxygen could provide a previously unrecognized connection between Earth's deep interior, volcanic activity, and the development of an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
The research was led by Dr. Yanhao Lin and Dr. Ho-kwang Mao of the Center for High Pressure Science and Technology Advanced Research (HPSTAR), working with Prof. Haiyang Niu of Northwestern Polytechnical University and Prof. Wim van Westrenen of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Their findings were published in National Science Review.
Scientists Challenge a Long-Standing Assumption About Magma
Oxygen is one of the most abundant elements inside Earth, accounting for more than half of the atoms in the planet's silicate interior. Silicates are minerals and molten materials composed primarily of silicon and oxygen, along with other elements. They make up much of Earth's mantle and crust.
Despite oxygen's abundance, scientists have traditionally assumed that magma can contain only a specific amount of it. Under this understanding, the oxygen content is determined by the quantities and electrical charge states of other elements in the molten rock, including silicon, magnesium, and iron.
Water and carbon dioxide behave differently. Both can dissolve in magma and later escape as gases when the surrounding pressure decreases. These substances are known as volatile components, and their release plays an important role in volcanic activity.
Oxygen, however, has generally not been treated as a separate volatile substance that magma can absorb and release. Whether molten silicate rock could hold additional oxygen independently of its ordinary chemical composition remained largely unexplored.
The new research suggests that this assumption may need to change.
Extreme Pressure Reveals Hidden Oxygen in Molten Rock
To investigate, the scientists recreated conditions found deep within Earth using laboratory equipment capable of generating extraordinary pressures and temperatures.
They heated a synthetic version of mid-ocean ridge basalt, a type of volcanic rock commonly produced where tectonic plates move apart beneath the oceans. The samples were exposed to pressures ranging from normal atmospheric pressure to 7 gigapascals and temperatures between 1200 and 1800 °C.
A pressure of 7 gigapascals is approximately 69,000 times the atmospheric pressure at Earth's surface.
The team used specialized piston-cylinder and cubic presses to maintain these extreme conditions. They also added platinum oxide (PtO2) to establish an oxygen-rich environment and test how much additional oxygen the molten rock could absorb.
After the experiments, the researchers rapidly cooled the molten material, producing glass that preserved important characteristics of the melt. They then analyzed its elemental composition and measured the amounts of water and carbon dioxide present.
By calculating how much oxygen was needed to balance the other elements, along with the oxygen already contained in water and carbon dioxide, the scientists could estimate how much remained unaccounted for.
They called this additional amount "excess oxygen."
The results revealed a striking relationship between pressure and oxygen storage.
At normal atmospheric pressure, the glass contained almost no excess oxygen. At 7 gigapascals, however, excess oxygen accounted for more than 5% of the sample's weight.
For comparison, experiments conducted at similar pressures and temperatures without added platinum oxide produced excess oxygen concentrations of only 0.2% to 0.5% by weight.
The researchers also wanted to determine whether the additional oxygen was truly incorporated into the material or merely trapped as tiny gas bubbles.
Using Raman spectroscopy, a technique that identifies substances by examining how they interact with light, they found no detectable signature of oxygen gas in the glass. This indicated that the excess oxygen had become part of the glass structure rather than accumulating in bubbles.
The measured concentrations may even underestimate magma's actual oxygen-storage capacity. Some oxygen could have escaped while the molten samples were cooling, meaning the original melts may have contained still greater amounts.
Computer Simulations Reveal How Magma Stores Extra Oxygen
To better understand the discovery at the atomic level, Prof. Niu led a series of theoretical computer simulations.
The researchers used deep neural network (DNN) models to simulate interactions among atoms with accuracy approaching that of ab initio calculations, which describe atomic behavior using fundamental principles of quantum mechanics.
The simulations showed that additional oxygen could dissolve into molten material until the system reached equilibrium, a state in which oxygen entering and leaving the melt is balanced.
Although the computer models used a simplified system containing only magnesium, silicon, and oxygen, they reproduced the same overall pattern observed in the laboratory: magma's ability to hold excess oxygen increased with pressure.
The simulated oxygen concentrations were lower than the experimental measurements, which the scientists attributed to differences between the simplified model and the more complex chemical composition of actual basalt.
The calculations also revealed changes in how oxygen atoms behaved as more oxygen entered the melt. Their electrical charges became more varied, and a small proportion formed peroxide-like bonds, in which oxygen atoms bond to one another.
These changes help explain how molten rock might accommodate oxygen beyond the amount predicted by conventional chemical models.
Importantly, the pressure-dependent behavior resembles that of water and carbon dioxide, which also become more soluble in magma as pressure increases.
Based on these findings, the researchers propose that oxygen should be recognized as an independent component of silicate melts, rather than being considered only in relation to other elements.
Could Ancient Volcanoes Have Helped Oxygenate Earth's Atmosphere?
The discovery raises a much larger question about Earth's history: Could magma have transported significant amounts of oxygen from the planet's interior to its surface?
The researchers suggest a possible mechanism involving magma generated in oxidized regions of Earth's mantle.
Under the immense pressures deep underground, this magma could absorb substantial quantities of excess oxygen. As it moves upward, the surrounding pressure decreases, reducing the amount of oxygen the molten rock can retain.
Some of that oxygen could then be released, potentially contributing to chemical reactions that increase the oxidation of the upper mantle, Earth's crust, and eventually the atmosphere.
Oxidation refers to chemical processes involving the transfer of electrons. In this context, oxygen carried by magma could increase the oxidizing capacity of surrounding materials and potentially influence the balance of oxygen in the atmosphere.
This proposed mechanism may also help explain an intriguing coincidence in Earth's geological past.
Between approximately 2.5 billion and 2.0 billion years ago, atmospheric oxygen levels underwent major increases. This interval overlaps with the formation of some of Earth's largest large igneous provinces (LIPs), enormous regions of volcanic rock created by exceptionally large outpourings of magma.
The researchers suggest that oxygen released from these ancient volcanic systems could have contributed to changes in atmospheric composition.
Their preliminary calculation highlights the potentially enormous scale of the process. They estimate that if magma erupted during this period released excess oxygen equal to just 0.27% of its weight, the total amount could theoretically match all the oxygen present in Earth's atmosphere today.
This does not establish that volcanic activity actually supplied that much atmospheric oxygen. Instead, it illustrates how even a relatively small release of oxygen from immense quantities of magma could have major planetary consequences.
A New Clue to Earth's Evolution and Habitable Planets
The findings could influence several important areas of planetary science.
For one, they may change how scientists understand ancient magma oceans, vast regions of molten rock believed to have existed during the early evolution of Earth and other rocky planets.
They also introduce a possible new factor in volcanic degassing, the process through which gases and other volatile substances escape from molten rock and interact with a planet's atmosphere.
If magma can store and release oxygen independently of its other chemical components, models of Earth's atmospheric development may need to account for this previously overlooked process.
The implications could extend beyond Earth. Understanding how oxygen moves between the interiors and atmospheres of rocky planets may help researchers investigate the conditions that allow potentially habitable environments to develop and persist over billions of years.
Although further research is needed to establish how much oxygen natural magmas carry and how much reaches the atmosphere, the discovery points to a surprising possibility: some of the processes that helped shape Earth's oxygen-rich environment may have originated far beneath the planet's surface.

Even before Trump launched the military campaign alongside Israel eight months ago, Vance had advocated more intensive diplomatic efforts. Trump subsequently appointed him to lead the U.S. negotiating team, and the vice president traveled twice to meet Iranian officials in an effort to reach a final agreement that would ease tensions.
According to the Journal, Washington's decision to elevate Rezaei as a central interlocutor could sideline other senior Iranian officials, including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.
The reported outreach follows an unusual diplomatic meeting earlier this week in Tehran, where senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian representatives, including Rezaei, in an attempt to reduce regional tensions. The talks took place as Yemen's Houthi movement launched renewed attacks against Saudi Arabia and Egypt approved defensive assistance to Riyadh.
Reuters noted that the meeting marked the first high-level talks between Iran and the three countries. Iran has previously been mentioned as a possible future participant in the Mecca Pact, a mutual defense arrangement involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey under which an attack on one member is considered an attack on all three. The agreement's effectiveness has come under scrutiny following Houthi attacks on Riyadh.

Judge rejects US Justice Dept bid to block votes from alleged noncitizens in California
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
02:10:24 CET
10:10:24 KST

By Luc Cohen, Andrew Goudsward and Nate Raymond
Oct 28 (Reuters) - A US judge strongly rebuked the Trump administration on Wednesday by rejecting a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting mail ballots for the midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the department alleges are likely noncitizens.
The decision marks the latest setback for President Donald Trump’s effort to boost the federal government’s role in elections ahead of the November 3 midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress.
US District Judge David Carter issued the decision after a hearing on Tuesday in Los Angeles federal court over the Justice Department’s request for a temporary restraining order barring officials from counting any ballots from the individuals it flagged.
The Justice Department’s lawsuit, filed on October 15, was a rare intervention in the voting process weeks before an election and signaled the Trump administration’s willingness to contest the midterm results in court.
“Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch,” Carter wrote on Wednesday.
The judge, an appointee of Democratic President Bill Clinton, said the Justice Department’s last-minute request to exclude over 20,000 ballots ran afoul of “longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections.”
Carter warned that a ruling in the Trump administration’s favor would “wreak havoc” and cause thousands of registered voters to “potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.”
“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable,” Carter wrote. “Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred. If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger.”
The Justice Department swiftly appealed the decision to the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals.
“Every day, more ballots are processed by election officials,” Justice Department lawyer Bill Essayli said in a statement. “This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution.”
California has said the state’s safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust. It said the Justice Department’s assertions relied on “suspect data” and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters.
California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives — 52 — than any other state.
Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its “sanctuary state” policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by noncitizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare.
APPEALS COURT REJECTED EMERGENCY REQUEST
Carter ruled two days after a federal appeals court on Monday rejected an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule.
The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot.
It had argued that a restraining order was necessary to ensure that California did not impede prosecutors’ ability to enforce a federal law that makes it illegal for noncitizens to vote in federal elections.
But Carter said the Justice Department never explained why counting ballots would impair any prosecutions under the law, as states are not required to help the federal government investigate and prosecute crimes.
Apart from California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states that are home to competitive races.
In Alaska, the Justice Department last week asked a judge to prevent certification of election results if the Republican incumbent senator loses by a slim margin, alleging that the presence of another candidate with a similar name on the ballot could confuse voters. Alaska has urged that the case be dismissed, arguing it has taken steps to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot.
In Washington state, the Justice Department on Monday sent a letter asking officials not to count any ballots received from 400 voters it said may not be citizens. Washington’s top elections official said the timing of the request indicated it was intended to cast unfounded suspicion on election results.
California had 23 million registered voters as of December 2025, while Washington had 5 million registered voters as of 2024, state records show.
Voting rights activists have expressed concern that the federal government’s methods for scrutinizing state voter lists to identify noncitizen voters risk wrongly flagging naturalized citizens for removal from the rolls.
(Reporting by Luc Cohen in New York, Nate Raymond in Boston and Andrew Goudsward in Washington; Editing by Nia Williams, Chizu Nomiyama, Stephen Coates and Saad Sayeed)
